records.name: Hyperalgesia
records.description: Increased pain response to stimuli that are normally painful, where the magnitude of pain exceeds what the stimulus warrants
records.body:
**Hyperalgesia** is an increased pain response to stimuli that are normally painful — the gain on pain is turned up, so that a mildly painful stimulus produces severe pain. Unlike [allodynia](./allodynia.md) (pain from non-painful stimuli), hyperalgesia involves stimuli that would produce some pain in anyone; the difference is in the magnitude of the response.

Hyperalgesia is classified by location relative to the original injury:

- **Primary hyperalgesia** — increased pain sensitivity at the site of tissue damage. This is partly driven by peripheral sensitization: inflammatory mediators lower nociceptor thresholds, so nerve fibers in the injured area fire more readily. The inflamed area around a cut or burn being exquisitely tender to touch is primary hyperalgesia.
- **Secondary hyperalgesia** — increased pain sensitivity in uninjured tissue surrounding the site of damage. This is driven by [central sensitization](./central-sensitization.md): the spinal cord amplifies signals from the broader region, not just from the injury site. The area around a burn being painful to light pressure, even where the skin is intact, is secondary hyperalgesia.

The clinical distinction matters. Primary hyperalgesia may respond to anti-inflammatory treatment targeting the peripheral sensitization. Secondary hyperalgesia will not — because the amplification is occurring centrally.

## Opioid-induced hyperalgesia

A particularly significant form is **opioid-induced hyperalgesia (OIH)** — a paradoxical state in which opioid use itself increases pain sensitivity. Rather than producing more analgesia, continued opioid exposure activates pronociceptive mechanisms (NMDA receptor activation, glial activation, descending facilitation) that amplify pain. The patient reports worsening pain, the clinician increases the opioid dose, the hyperalgesia worsens, the dose increases again — a cycle that can produce severe, widespread pain driven entirely by the treatment intended to relieve it.

OIH is clinically distinct from tolerance (which requires more drug to achieve the same effect) and from disease progression (which involves worsening of the underlying condition). It is one of the mechanisms through which the opioid crisis has harmed chronic pain patients — patients whose pain worsened precisely because of the medications prescribed to manage it, then faced dose reductions that produced withdrawal on top of iatrogenic hyperalgesia.

This dynamic connects directly to [harm reduction](../../../../../public-health-services-section/content/text/glossary/terms/harm-reduction.md). Patients experiencing OIH need careful, compassionate dose management — not abrupt discontinuation (which produces withdrawal and rebound pain) and not dose escalation (which worsens the hyperalgesia). The harm reduction principle of meeting people where they are, reducing immediate danger, and treating survival as the first priority applies directly to opioid taper in hyperalgesic patients.

## Related terms

- [Allodynia](./allodynia.md) — pain from non-painful stimuli (the companion concept)
- [Central Sensitization](./central-sensitization.md) — the mechanism driving secondary hyperalgesia
- [Nociception](./nociception.md) — the peripheral process that hyperalgesia amplifies
- [Chronic Pain](./chronic-pain.md) — the condition in which hyperalgesia is commonly observed

records.name: Idiotypic Network Theory
records.description: Niels Jerne's 1974 theory that the immune repertoire forms a self-referential regulatory network — antibodies bear unique variable-region shapes (idiotopes) that other antibodies (anti-idiotypes) can themselves recognize and bind.
records.body:
The idiotypic network theory, proposed by Niels Kaj Jerne in "Towards a Network Theory of the Immune System" (1974) [@jerne1974], observes that an antibody's variable (antigen-binding) region is itself a molecular shape — and therefore is itself potentially antigenic. The unique features of that shape are called idiotopes, collectively an antibody's idiotype. Jerne's proposal: the immune system contains antibodies (anti-idiotypes) that recognize the idiotopes of other antibodies, and those anti-idiotypes are in turn recognized by further anti-anti-idiotypes, and so on — an internally connected network of antibodies binding antibodies, not just antibodies binding external antigen.

## What the theory explains

- **Regulation without external input** — because idiotype/anti-idiotype pairs can suppress or amplify each other's activity, the network can in principle regulate immune responses (dampening an antibody population once it has expanded, for instance) without waiting for antigen to disappear.
- **Internal images** — an anti-idiotype antibody, by binding the idiotope of an antibody raised against a real antigen, can end up structurally resembling that original antigen. Jerne proposed this as a mechanism by which the network could carry an "internal image" of antigens the body has encountered, and even suggested anti-idiotype antibodies as a route to vaccine design (immunizing with an anti-idiotype instead of the pathogen antigen itself).
- **A repertoire that is never fully at rest** — under network theory, the immune system is not a passive detector waiting for foreign antigen; idiotype and anti-idiotype populations are already interacting with each other in the antigen-free state, so the system has an internal dynamic independent of external challenge.

## Reception

Jerne received the 1984 Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine substantially for this and related work on immune regulation. Despite the prize, network theory was progressively marginalized within mainstream immunology over the following decades — clonal selection and (later) the danger model proved more experimentally tractable and better supported by direct evidence, while idiotypic network effects, though real, turned out to play a smaller regulatory role than Jerne's strong formulation proposed. Part of the theory's difficulty was structural rather than empirical: describing a genuinely self-referential network (antibodies recognizing antibodies recognizing antibodies) in a way precise enough to generate testable quantitative predictions is a hard mathematical problem, and the immunology of the 1970s–80s did not have a ready formalism for it.

## A framing from outside immunology

The founding note for this section's theory arc singles out idiotypic network theory as an instance of a pattern this vault's estate claims a formalism for: "identity constituted by arrows on arrows, Yoneda with lymphocytes" — reading Jerne's network as a category-theoretic structure (a system defined by its relations to other instances of itself) rather than as a metaphor, and citing the theory's marginalization as partly a mathematics gap rather than an empirical refutation. See ["Immunity as Belief Board"](../../../../../../../../../../../../content/text/documents/articles/notes/2026/08/21/2026-08-21-note-on-immunity-as-belief-board.md), and the vault's [obsmetrological](../../../../../../../../../math-services-section/services/obsmetrological-services-section/apps/pymetrologic/docs/THEORY.md) framework the note draws on. Both are offered as a candidate reading, not as an established resolution of why the theory was marginalized.

## Related terms

- [Antibody](./antibody.md) — the molecule whose variable region idiotypic network theory treats as itself antigenic
- [Danger model](./danger-model.md) — the competing account that displaced much of network theory's explanatory territory
- [Self/non-self discrimination](./self-non-self.md) — the classification network theory reframes as internally, not only externally, determined

records.name: Immunological Tolerance
records.description: The set of mechanisms by which the immune system withholds attack from self-antigens, commensal microbiota, food antigens, and (during pregnancy) fetal antigens — despite these being detectable as non-self.
records.body:
Immunological tolerance is not merely the absence of an antigen the immune system could react to — it is an active, ongoing classification: some detectable non-self material is treated as something other than a threat. This is the harder half of self/non-self discrimination. Building a repertoire capable of recognizing foreign antigen is comparatively simple (random receptor generation supplies it for free); the difficult engineering problem is preventing that repertoire from firing on the body's own tissue, its symbiotic microbiota, ingested food proteins, and — for roughly nine months at a time in placental mammals — a genetically distinct fetus.

## Mechanisms

- **Central tolerance** — deletion or inactivation of self-reactive lymphocyte clones during development, in the thymus (T cells) and bone marrow (B cells). See [self/non-self discrimination](./self-non-self.md).
- **Peripheral tolerance** — mechanisms acting on mature lymphocytes that escaped central deletion:
  - **Regulatory T cells (Tregs)** — a dedicated T cell subset (CD4+CD25+FoxP3+) that actively suppresses immune responses via inhibitory cytokines (IL-10, TGF-β) and direct cell contact, rather than merely failing to respond.
  - **Anergy** — a state of functional unresponsiveness induced when a T cell receptor engages antigen without the accompanying costimulatory signal that antigen-presenting cells provide only in the presence of danger or inflammation cues.
  - **Clonal ignorance** — antigens that are physically inaccessible to circulating lymphocytes (immune-privileged sites: eye, testis, brain) never trigger a response because they are never encountered, not because tolerance was actively established.
- **Oral tolerance** — the gut immune system is specifically biased toward generating regulatory responses to ingested antigens, suppressing reaction to food proteins and commensal bacteria that would otherwise provoke inflammation at a surface constantly exposed to foreign material.
- **Maternal-fetal tolerance** — pregnancy involves active local suppression at the maternal-fetal interface (regulatory T cell expansion, altered antigen presentation, complement regulation) rather than the fetus's paternal antigens simply going undetected.

## Failure modes

When tolerance mechanisms fail on self-antigen, the result is [autoimmunity](./autoimmunity.md). When they fail on food or environmental antigen, the result is allergy. Both are failures of the same regulatory apparatus directed at different targets — which is part of why classification of the failure matters as much as detection of the failure.

## A framing from outside immunology

The founding note for this section's theory arc proposes reading tolerance as a specific classification outcome: "commensal and food antigens carry nonzero raw conflict yet are correctly filed as residual uncertainty rather than named conflicts." On that reading, tolerance is not the absence of a signal but a deliberate downgrading of a real signal to a non-actionable category — and autoimmunity is what happens when that downgrading fails. See ["Immunity as Belief Board"](../../../../../../../../../../../../content/text/documents/articles/notes/2026/08/21/2026-08-21-note-on-immunity-as-belief-board.md) for the full argument, offered there as a draft hypothesis awaiting review rather than as an immunology finding.

## Related terms

- [Self/non-self discrimination](./self-non-self.md) — the classification tolerance maintains
- [Autoimmunity](./autoimmunity.md) — the clinical failure mode when tolerance to self breaks down
- [Danger model](./danger-model.md) — an account of why tolerance and response are keyed to damage signals rather than antigen identity alone

records.description: A research-coordination umbrella for chronic symptom clusters appearing after infection with diverse pathogens, grouped to enable cross-condition hypothesis testing and shared research infrastructure despite mechanistic uncertainty.

records.body:
## Definition and scope

**Infection-associated chronic illness** (IACI) is a research-coordination and funding term, not a diagnostic category or a claim of shared disease mechanism.
The term groups chronic symptom clusters that appear following infection with diverse pathogens — long COVID (PASC), myalgic encephalomyelitis/chronic fatigue syndrome (ME/CFS), post-treatment Lyme disease syndrome (PTLDS), post-Ebola syndrome, post-dengue syndrome, and post-SARS-1 chronic illness — for the purposes of pooling research infrastructure, harmonizing outcome measures, and enabling hypothesis testing across conditions too individually rare or geographically dispersed to study at adequate statistical power.

The National Academies of Sciences, Engineering, and Medicine formalized the term in 2024, defining long COVID explicitly as "an infection-associated chronic condition occurring after SARS-CoV-2 infection that is present for at least 3 months as a continuous, relapsing and remitting, or progressive disease state that can present as singular or multiple symptoms and/or diagnosable conditions."
The umbrella framing originated in the earlier scientific literature as "post-acute infection syndromes" (PAIS), proposed by Choutka and colleagues in 2022 to describe the observation that symptoms following diverse infections showed "relatively similar symptom profiles... irrespective of the infectious agent."

### Important distinction: PAIS versus IACC/IACI

The term carries two related but distinct lineages.
**Post-acute infection syndromes (PAIS)** is the scientific framing: a hypothesis that these conditions share overlapping symptom patterns and warrant unified research attention.
**Infection-associated chronic condition/illness (IACC/IACI)** is the 2024 policy and funding language adopted by NASEM and NIH to operationalize that hypothesis.
This document discusses both, but the distinction matters: PAIS is a proposed scientific class based on symptom convergence; IACC is a governance term used to coordinate research funding and infrastructure.

### A research lens, not a settled entity

This is explicitly a research lens, not evidence of one disease.
IACC groups conditions for methodological purposes — enabling trials to harmonize outcome measures across structurally different infections, allowing biobank and cohort infrastructure to serve multiple conditions, and creating the statistical power needed to test mechanistic hypotheses that cannot be powered in single rare conditions.
As the NASEM 2024 workshop proceedings state explicitly, treating these conditions as one research class is a STRATEGY for improving research design, not a claim that they are one pathophysiology.

Whether these conditions share a common mechanism, several convergent mechanisms, or are etiologically distinct conditions that happen to produce overlapping symptom clusters because fatigue, post-exertional malaise, and cognitive impairment are downstream expressions of many different types of insults — this remains the central open question the research agenda exists to address.
No study to date has identified a single biomarker, causal pathway, or diagnostic test present across all six named conditions.

## Shared phenomenology

Despite their distinct infectious triggers, the named conditions share overlapping core symptoms, documented independently in multiple cohorts:

- **Fatigue not relieved by rest** — present across long COVID, ME/CFS, PTLDS, post-Ebola, post-dengue, and post-SARS-1 cohorts
- **Post-exertional malaise (PEM)** — disproportionate and delayed worsening of symptoms following physical, cognitive, or emotional exertion, documented in long COVID and ME/CFS cohorts; present in post-SARS-1 chronic syndrome
- **Cognitive impairment** — variously described as "brain fog," memory impairment, or attentional dysfunction, documented in long COVID, ME/CFS, and post-SARS-1 survivors
- **Autonomic symptoms** — orthostatic intolerance, POTS-like symptoms, dysautonomia, reported in long COVID and ME/CFS cohorts

### Long COVID / Post-acute COVID-19 (PASC)

Global prevalence: Wulf Hanson and colleagues' 2022 Global Burden of Disease analysis estimated ~6.2% of symptomatic COVID-19 cases developed one of three studied symptom clusters (fatigue, cognitive, respiratory) at 3 months post-infection; the same group estimated ~144.7 million individuals had developed long COVID by end of 2021, with ~15.1% (~22 million) remaining symptomatic at 12 months.
The RECOVER-Adult cohort (n=9,764) developed a consensus case definition distinguishing long COVID from baseline chronic disease or other diagnoses, establishing the phenomenological foundation for the term.

### Myalgic encephalomyelitis/chronic fatigue syndrome (ME/CFS)

Established case definitions exist (IOM 2015, Canadian Consensus Criteria 2003), mandating post-exertional malaise as a cardinal feature.
The core diagnostic triad is fatigue lasting >6 months not relieved by rest, post-exertional malaise, and unrefreshing sleep.
Clinical prevalence is estimated at 836,000 to 2.5 million in the US (IOM 2015); the wide range reflects definitional heterogeneity in epidemiological studies.

### Overlap between long COVID and ME/CFS

A 2024 systematic review and meta-analysis by Dehlia and Guthridge pooling data from 13 studies (n=1,973 long-COVID patients) found that 51% (95% CI 42–60%) of long-COVID patients met ME/CFS diagnostic criteria, establishing substantial phenomenological overlap between the two conditions in the same patients.

### Post-treatment Lyme disease syndrome (PTLDS)

Defined as persisting pain, fatigue, or cognitive impairment following antibiotic-cleared *Borrelia burgdorferi* infection.
Prevalence estimates range from 10–20% of optimally treated patients in multiple cohort studies, with fatigue being the most frequent persistent symptom (~39% at 6 months in standardized-measure cohorts).
The pathophysiology of PTLDS remains unknown.

### Post-Ebola syndrome

The PREVAIL III prospective cohort study (n=966 Ebola-antibody-positive survivors vs. 2,350 antibody-negative contacts, ~90% followed 12 months) tracked six symptoms significantly elevated in survivors versus contacts: urinary frequency, headache, fatigue, muscle pain, memory loss, and joint pain.
All six declined during follow-up.
Uveitis was the sole exception, rising from 26.4% in survivors at baseline to 33.3% by year 1.

### Post-dengue fatigue syndrome

Approximately 20–25% of hospitalized dengue-fever patients in cohort studies report significant fatigue at 2 months post-infection, establishing post-dengue fatigue syndrome as a common post-viral sequela.

### Post-SARS (SARS-CoV-1, 2003) chronic syndrome

The 2009 Archives of Internal Medicine study by Lam and colleagues found that 27.1% of 233 SARS survivors met modified 1994 CDC chronic fatigue syndrome criteria at a mean follow-up of 41.3 months (approximately 3.4 years) after infection, documenting long-term disability in a substantial fraction of survivors.
This finding predates long COVID by over a decade and is the historical precedent explicitly cited in recent long-COVID/ME-CFS overlap literature.

## Why the class framing matters for research design

NASEM 2024 and Choutka et al. 2022 state the methodological rationale explicitly:

1. **Statistical power through pooling** — each individual condition (PTLDS, post-dengue, post-Ebola, post-SARS-1) has historically been too rare or too temporally/geographically isolated to support well-powered biomarker research or clinical trials.
  Grouping them allows shared case definitions, outcome measures, and research infrastructure to serve multiple conditions simultaneously.

2. **Long COVID as a research engine** — the much larger patient population (tens of millions) and dramatically increased funding for long COVID (the NIH RECOVER initiative allocated ~$1 billion) creates unprecedented opportunity to test hypotheses about autonomic dysfunction, viral persistence, EBV reactivation, autoimmunity, and microbiome dysbiosis at a scale previously impossible for ME/CFS or PTLDS alone.
  Findings generated at this scale can then be tested for transfer to the smaller, under-resourced conditions.

3. **Harmonized measurement frameworks** — a shared symptom-based case definition and unified outcome-measure set (validated instruments for post-exertional malaise, cognitive impairment, autonomic dysfunction) allow trials to compare results across studies despite different infectious triggers, creating a common evidence base where none existed.

4. **Historical precedent argument** — the post-SARS-1 chronic-illness literature (Lam 2009, Moldofsky 2011) was a small, underfunded area of research for over a decade.
  The 2022–2024 framing of PAIS and IACC explicitly cites this history to argue against treating each new infectious agent (dengue, Ebola, COVID-19) as an unprecedented phenomenon requiring research to restart from zero each time.
  The recurrence of the pattern across pathogens is itself evidence for taking the class perspective seriously.

## What is not yet established: mechanism

The NASEM 2024 workshop chapter "Common Mechanistic Factors of Infection-Associated Chronic Illnesses" documents the following status:

### Hypothesized mechanisms under active investigation

- **Viral persistence or latent reactivation** — SARS-CoV-2 RNA has been detected in tissue reservoirs; EBV reactivation is documented in some long-COVID cohorts.
  Su and colleagues' 2022 study of 309 COVID-19 patients identified four early factors predicting progression to PASC, including SARS-CoV-2 RNAemia and EBV viremia.
  However, the NASEM workshop explicitly notes that "whether EBV infection is associated with developing ME/CFS, or whether the chronic illness is creating an environment where EBV can reactivate" remains unresolved — direction of causation is not established.

- **Autoimmunity and molecular mimicry** — elevated autoantibodies (against ACE2, β2-adrenoceptors, M2 muscarinic receptors, and other targets) are associated with long COVID in multiple cohorts.
  A causal or diagnostic role remains unproven.

- **Autonomic nervous system dysfunction** — POTS-type symptoms and orthostatic intolerance are common findings in long-COVID and ME/CFS cohorts.
  These are established as co-occurring phenomena but not established as the primary root mechanism.

- **Microclots and endotheliopathy** — fibrinaloid microclots in platelet-poor plasma have been reported in long-COVID and ME/CFS cohorts.
  This finding remains contested and is not yet replicated at the scale and rigor required for firm establishment.

- **Microbiome dysbiasis and neuroinflammation** — altered bacterial composition and metabolic dysfunction (particularly dopamine and glutamate metabolism pathways) have been documented.
  Status: mechanistic hypothesis, early-stage research.

### Explicitly unresolved

- Direction of causality between viral reactivation and chronic-illness state
- The mechanism by which different infectious agents produce similar phenotypes
- Whether the conditions share one underlying mechanism, several convergent mechanisms, or are etiologically distinct conditions whose symptom overlap reflects common downstream effects of different insults
- Causal versus correlative roles for any candidate biomarker (autoantibodies, microclots, metabolic markers)

## Clinical implications

For clinical research: the critical consequence is that studies of a single condition cannot be directly compared without explicit statement of case definitions used.
Findings in Fukuda-defined ME/CFS patients (focused on fatigue) are not directly comparable to findings in IOM-defined ME/CFS patients (mandating post-exertional malaise), and neither is directly comparable to findings in PASC cohorts that use yet another case definition.

For trial design: the IACC grouping enables outcome-measure harmonization, allowing future trials to build a comparable evidence base.
It does not settle what should be treated, how, or whether the same interventions work across all six conditions.

## Related terms

- [Myalgic encephalomyelitis](../../../../services/myalgic-encephalomyelitis-services-section/content/text/glossary/terms/myalgic-encephalomyelitis.md) — one condition grouped under the IACC umbrella, characterized by post-exertional malaise as the cardinal feature
- [Post-exertional malaise](../../../../services/myalgic-encephalomyelitis-services-section/content/text/glossary/terms/post-exertional-malaise.md) — the symptom most consistent across IACC conditions
- Long COVID / Post-acute COVID-19 sequelae — the condition that provided the statistical power and research funding enabling the IACC framing to emerge
- Autoimmunity — a candidate mechanistic factor under active investigation across IACC conditions
- Post-viral syndrome — the broader historical category of chronic illness following infection, of which IACC conditions are a contemporary subset

records.name: Interleukin-1 beta
records.description: The inflammasome-processed member of the interleukin-1 family, synthesized as an inactive precursor and requiring caspase-1 cleavage before release, making its activity gated by a second signal rather than by transcription alone.

dinarello2009.title: Immunological and Inflammatory Functions of the Interleukin-1 Family
dinarello2009.note: PMID 19302047; resolved against CrossRef and PubMed 2026-09-02

hayden2008.title: Shared Principles in NF-κB Signaling
hayden2008.note: PMID 18267068; resolved against CrossRef and PubMed 2026-09-02

zell1997.title: TNF-alpha and IL-1 alpha inhibit both pyruvate dehydrogenase activity and mitochondrial function in cardiomyocytes: evidence for primary impairment of mitochondrial function

records.body:
Interleukin-1 beta is a member of the interleukin-1 family synthesized as an inactive precursor whose release requires inflammasome assembly and caspase-1 cleavage, after which it acts on the type I interleukin-1 receptor to induce fever, hyperalgesia, and further inflammatory transcription [dinarello2009]. Transcription of the precursor is NF-κB-dependent [hayden2008; dinarello2009], the **produced-by** relation asserted here (**established**).

Its activity is gated at two steps rather than one — transcription of the precursor and then proteolytic activation — which distinguishes it from cytokines released as soon as they are transcribed and means precursor abundance does not predict activity. **Established**: the two-signal requirement is the organizing fact of the interleukin-1 literature.

The **impairs** relation to oxidative phosphorylation is sourced in Zell and colleagues, whose cardiomyocyte experiments used interleukin-1 alpha alongside tumour necrosis factor alpha and found inhibition of both pyruvate dehydrogenase activity and mitochondrial function [zell1997]. **Single in-vitro study, and with the family member alpha rather than beta**: the extension to interleukin-1 beta is inference from shared receptor signalling, not a result reported in that work.

Measuring this cytokine in serum therefore underestimates the local inflammatory state, because the biologically decisive step happens in tissue and the mature protein is short-lived in circulation.

records.name: Interleukin-6
records.description: A pleiotropic cytokine induced by NF-κB that drives the acute-phase response and, through soluble-receptor trans-signalling, acts on cells that carry no membrane receptor of its own; both a pro-inflammatory messenger and a myokine released by contracting muscle.

tanaka2014.title: IL-6 in Inflammation, Immunity, and Disease
tanaka2014.publication: Cold Spring Harbor Perspectives in Biology
tanaka2014.note: PMID 25190079; resolved against CrossRef and PubMed 2026-09-02

hayden2008.title: Shared Principles in NF-κB Signaling
hayden2008.note: PMID 18267068; resolved against CrossRef and PubMed 2026-09-02

records.body:
Interleukin-6 is a cytokine induced downstream of NF-κB activation that drives the hepatic acute-phase response, supports antibody production, and acts on the central nervous system to produce fever and sickness behaviour [tanaka2014]. Its gene is a canonical target of the NF-κB pathway [hayden2008], which is the relation this carrier asserts as **produced-by** (**established**).

It differs from most cytokines in having two signalling modes: classic signalling through membrane-bound IL-6 receptor, restricted to hepatocytes and some leukocytes, and trans-signalling through a soluble receptor complex that reaches any cell bearing gp130 [tanaka2014]. **Established**: the two modes and their different target populations are the organizing distinction of the modern IL-6 literature.

A serum concentration therefore does not determine the effect: the same level acts on a restricted or an unrestricted cell population depending on how much soluble receptor is present, so this cytokine cannot be read as a single-number index of inflammation. For research reading a person's inflammatory state over time, the consequence is that a stable concentration is compatible with a changing biological effect, and that comparisons across studies which measure only total concentration are comparing weaker quantities than they appear to.

records.name: Intermittent Explosive Disorder
records.description: A DSM-IV/DSM-5 diagnosis for recurrent, discrete episodes of impulsive, anger-driven aggression grossly out of proportion to any precipitating stressor, found in a U.S. national survey to affect a lifetime 7.3% of adults with mean onset at age 14.

kessler2006.title: The prevalence and correlates of DSM-IV intermittent explosive disorder in the National Comorbidity Survey Replication

records.body:
Intermittent explosive disorder (IED) is defined by recurrent, discrete episodes of impulsive aggression — verbal or physical outbursts grossly out of proportion to whatever provoked them — rather than by a standing, between-episode mood disturbance. In the National Comorbidity Survey Replication (NCS-R), a nationally representative, face-to-face household survey of 9,282 U.S. adults age 18+ conducted 2001-2003 using the WHO Composite International Diagnostic Interview, Kessler, Coccaro, Fava, and colleagues (2006) found a lifetime IED prevalence of 7.3% and a 12-month prevalence of 3.9% — far higher than had previously been recognized. Cases reported a mean of 43 lifetime attacks and a mean of $1,359 in lifetime property damage, injuries occurred at a rate of 180 per 100 lifetime cases, and mean age at onset was 14.

IED should be distinguished from disruptive mood dysregulation disorder, the pediatric diagnosis covering chronic irritability. Where DMDD requires a chronic, non-episodic irritable or angry mood present most days between outbursts, IED is defined purely by the discrete episodes themselves, with no required background mood disturbance, and its epidemiology here describes the adult general population rather than children — the two are related but explicitly distinct constructs, and this survey's findings say nothing about IED's prevalence or presentation in children or adolescents.

Despite the disorder's early onset (mean age 14) and heavy associated burden, treatment contact specific to anger was rare: of people meeting lifetime IED criteria, 60.3% had at some point sought treatment for some emotional or substance problem, but only 28.8% had ever received anger-specific treatment, and only 11.7% of 12-month cases had received anger-specific treatment in the past year — a gap the authors call a target for early detection and outreach. Methodologically, these are retrospective self-report estimates from a single national survey using structured, lay-administered diagnostic interviews rather than clinician-confirmed diagnoses; the reported mean of 43 lifetime attacks and the dollar-figure property-damage estimate are recall-dependent and should not be read as precise counts. A widely repeated secondary claim that the 7.3% lifetime figure reflects a broad definition (three or more lifetime impulsive-anger attacks) against a narrower 5.4% figure (three or more attacks within one year) could not be traced to the primary abstract's own wording and is reported here only as an unverified secondary characterization, not a confirmed primary-source distinction.

records.body:
Interoception is the sense of the body's internal physiological state.
Where [proprioception](./proprioception.md) tells you where your body is in space, interoception tells you what's happening inside it: heart rate, breathing depth, gut motility, bladder fullness, temperature, hunger, thirst, and the diffuse signals of autonomic arousal that underlie what gets called "feeling."
[A.D. Craig](../../../../../../../../../../../information-science-services-section/services/knowledge-services-section/services/research-services-section/content/text/documents/articles/notes/a-d-craig.md) argued that interoception constitutes the physiological basis for subjective feeling states — it's how the body knows its own condition [@craig2002].

## Neuroanatomy of interoception

Interoceptive signals travel through two primary pathways:

**The lamina I spinothalamocortical pathway** carries signals from small-diameter afferent fibers (C and Aδ fibers) throughout the body.
These fibers respond to temperature, tissue damage, metabolic state, visceral distension, and other physiological conditions.
Their signals ascend through lamina I of the spinal dorsal horn to the ventromedial posterior nucleus of the thalamus, then project to the posterior and mid-insular cortex [@craig2002].

**The vagal pathway** carries signals from visceral organs — heart, lungs, gut, liver — through the vagus nerve to the nucleus of the solitary tract (NTS) in the brainstem, then to the parabrachial nucleus and onward to the insular cortex.
[Stephen Porges](../../../../../../../../../../../information-science-services-section/services/knowledge-services-section/services/research-services-section/content/text/documents/articles/notes/stephen-porges.md)' polyvagal theory describes how vagal afferent activity shapes not just autonomic regulation but social behavior and emotional experience [@porges2011].

Both pathways converge on the **insular cortex**, particularly the anterior insula, which Craig identified as the site where raw physiological signals are integrated into a coherent representation of the body's current state — what he called the "sentient self."

## Interoceptive accuracy, sensibility, and awareness

Research distinguishes three dimensions of interoception [citation needed]:

**Interoceptive accuracy** — how well a person's subjective report matches objective measurement.
The heartbeat detection task is the classic measure: you count your heartbeats without taking a pulse, and researchers compare your count to actual cardiac output.
Accuracy varies across individuals and correlates with emotional sensitivity and anxiety regulation.

**Interoceptive sensibility** — a person's self-reported tendency to attend to interoceptive signals.
High sensibility doesn't guarantee high accuracy; some people believe they're attuned to their bodies but aren't measurably so.

**Interoceptive awareness** — the metacognitive dimension: how well a person's confidence in their interoceptive judgments tracks their actual accuracy.
High awareness means your confidence calibrates to your performance.

These distinctions matter clinically.
Anxiety disorders often involve high interoceptive sensibility (hypervigilance to bodily signals) coupled with low accuracy (misinterpreting those signals).
Dissociative conditions often involve low sensibility — a blunting of interoceptive input that reduces the felt sense of inhabiting a body.

## Interoception and affect

Craig's proposal — that interoception generates feeling states — has been supported by neuroimaging and clinical evidence.
The anterior insula activates during experiences of disgust, pain, empathy, and uncertainty.
Damage to the insula impairs the ability to recognize one's own emotional states, not just the ability to detect physiological signals.

This connects interoception to the vault's work on [affect](../../../../../../../../../../../philosophy-services-section/services/relationality-services-section/services/agency-services-section/content/text/documents/articles/notes/undated/affect.md).
If affect operates at the level of bodily potential — the capacity to act and be acted upon — then interoception is the sensory channel through which affect registers.
The felt quality of anxiety, excitement, fatigue, or ease isn't an interpretation layered on top of a neutral body; it's the body's own report of its autonomic and metabolic state.
Somatic practices that train interoceptive acuity don't just improve body awareness — they change the resolution at which affect is experienced.

## Interoception and information-theoretic stability

The [neurophysiological embodiment of information-theoretic stability](../../../../../../../neuroscience-services-section/content/text/documents/articles/notes/neurophysiological-embodiment-of-information-theoretic-stability.md) describes autonomic regulation as precision-weighted descent on free energy.
Interoceptive signals provide the error terms in this process: the difference between predicted and actual physiological state drives corrective autonomic responses.
High interoceptive accuracy means the prediction-error signal is clean; low accuracy means the system operates on noisy data, which degrades stability.

This formalization connects somatic practice to the vault's information-theoretic framework.
Training interoceptive acuity — through breathwork, body scanning, or [somatic experiencing](./somatic-experiencing.md) — doesn't just produce subjective calm.
It improves the precision of the signals that autonomic regulation depends on, moving the system toward the stability manifold that the information-theoretic model describes.

## Related concepts

- [Proprioception](./proprioception.md) — the complementary sense of body position in space
- [Somatic Awareness](./somatic-awareness.md) — the integrative capacity that draws on both interoception and proprioception
- [Somatic Experiencing](./somatic-experiencing.md) — a trauma approach that works through interoceptive tracking
- [Reiki](../../reiki/index.md) — a healing practice in which practitioners attend to interoceptive and energetic signals during treatment

## Sources

- Craig, A.D. (2002).
  "How do you feel?
  Interoception: the sense of the physiological condition of the body."
  *Nature Reviews Neuroscience*, 3(8), 655–666 [@craig2002].
- Porges, S.W. (2011).
  *The Polyvagal Theory.*
  Norton [@porges2011].
- Senn, E.
  (2025b).
  *Stability Dynamics in Cognitive Systems: A Predictive-Processing Interpretation.* arXiv:cs.
  AI [@senn2025b].

records.name: Irritability
records.description: A low threshold for anger, frustration, or annoyance that the research literature uses to name two related but distinct phenomena: a dimensional trait-level proneness and a bounded episode- or state-level presentation, each measured and validated differently.

perlis2005.title: Prevalence and clinical correlates of irritability in major depressive disorder: a preliminary report from the Sequenced Treatment Alternatives to Relieve Depression (STAR*D) study

perlis2009.title: Irritability is associated with anxiety and greater severity, but not bipolar spectrum features, in major depressive disorder

stringaris2012ari.title: The Affective Reactivity Index: a concise irritability scale for clinical and research settings
stringaris2012ari.publication: Journal of Child Psychology and Psychiatry

stringaris2012twin.title: Adolescent irritability: phenotypic associations and genetic links with depressed mood

copeland2013dmdd.title: Prevalence, comorbidity, and correlates of DSM-5 proposed disruptive mood dysregulation disorder

brotman2017.title: Irritability in youths: a translational model

records.body:
Irritability is a low threshold for anger, frustration, or annoyance in response to provocation, but the single word covers two distinguishable phenomena in the clinical and research literature. In its trait sense, irritability is a dimensional, relatively stable disposition — a proneness to anger that a person carries across situations and over time, the sense used when Leibenluft, Stringaris, and Brotman describe irritability as a transdiagnostic dimension cutting across depressive, anxiety, and disruptive-behavior presentations in youth, and the sense the Affective Reactivity Index is built to quantify. In its episode or state sense, irritability names a bounded period during which the trait manifests — the "present at least half the preceding week" operationalization used in the STAR*D depression trial (Perlis and colleagues), or the chronic, "most days" mood criterion in disruptive mood dysregulation disorder, which itself couples that tonic-mood requirement to a separate, phasic criterion of discrete temper outbursts. That DSM-5 category requiring both a chronic mood state and frequent discrete outbursts under one label is itself evidence that the literature has not settled on one word for one phenomenon.

Irritability, in either sense, should be distinguished from an anger attack, a more narrowly defined research construct: a discrete, situationally disproportionate episode of anger with autonomic or panic-like features (tachycardia, sweating, flushing, subjective loss of control) studied as a subgroup phenomenon within major depressive disorder. An anger attack is always episodic and always autonomically marked; irritability, by contrast, can be a stable trait with no discrete autonomic episode at all, and even in its episode sense (an outburst, a period of elevated irritable mood) need not carry the panic-attack-like somatic signature that defines an anger attack.

The consequence for research design is that prevalence and correlational findings reported under the single word "irritability" are not directly comparable across studies unless the sense being measured is specified. STAR*D's approximately 40-46% adult prevalence figures (Perlis and colleagues, 2005 and 2009) describe a state-level threshold — present at least half of the preceding week — in a treatment-seeking depressed adult cohort, cross-sectional and not a claim about stable trait level. DMDD's community prevalence of well under 5% after early childhood (Copeland, Angold, Costello, and Egger, 2013, in children and adolescents ages 2-17) describes categorical diagnostic caseness combining the tonic-mood and phasic-outburst criteria. And a genetic correlation of 0.70 between irritability and depressed mood found in a UK twin/sibling sample of adolescents (Stringaris, Zavos, Leibenluft, Maughan, and Eley, 2012) describes the dimensional trait as captured by parent-report instruments in youth. Treating these as one number describing one phenomenon would conflate a self-reported symptom-week threshold in depressed adults, a categorical pediatric diagnosis, and a dimensional trait score in adolescent twins — three different measurement operations that happen to share a name.

records.name: Body Fluids (Jin Ye)
records.description: 津液 — the normal physiological fluids of the body in TCM, comprising thin clear jin (sweat, tears, saliva) and thick nourishing ye (joint fluid, marrow, cerebrospinal fluid) — a fundamental substance alongside Qi, Blood, and Jing

kaptchuk2000.title: The Web That Has No Weaver

records.body:
Body fluids (jin ye 津液) are the normal physiological fluids of the body in [Traditional Chinese Medicine](traditional-chinese-medicine.md) — all fluids other than [Blood](xue.md).
Together with [Qi](qi.md), Blood, and [Jing](jing.md), they constitute the fundamental substances that the body needs to function.
Jin Ye moisten the skin, lubricate the joints, nourish the brain, fill the eyes and ears, and maintain the suppleness of all tissues.

## Jin and Ye

TCM distinguishes two subtypes:

**Jin** (津, "thin fluids"): Light, clear, watery, and mobile.
Jin circulates on the body's surface and in the muscles, moistening the skin and filling the orifices.
Sweat, tears, saliva, nasal mucus, and the fluid portion of urine are manifestations of Jin.
Jin moves with [Wei Qi](wei-qi.md) (defensive Qi) on the surface.

**Ye** (液, "thick fluids"): Dense, heavy, viscous, and slow-moving.
Ye circulates in the interior, lubricating joints, moistening the brain and spinal cord, nourishing bone marrow, and filling the sensory organs.
Synovial fluid, cerebrospinal fluid, and the vitreous humor of the eye are manifestations of Ye.
Ye is closely related to [Jing](jing.md) and [Blood](xue.md) — all three are Yin substances that nourish in depth.

## Metabolism of body fluids

The production, distribution, and excretion of body fluids involves three organ systems:

- **Spleen**: Transforms ingested fluids from food and drink into usable Jin Ye (the "source of fluids")
- **Lung**: Distributes fluids to the surface (skin, pores) and directs excess fluids downward to the Kidney
- **Kidney**: Governs water metabolism, separating clear (recycled) from turbid (excreted as urine).
  The Kidney's [Yang](yang-deficiency.md) provides the metabolic fire that drives fluid transformation

When this system functions normally, fluids are produced, distributed, and excreted in balance.
When it fails — through Spleen deficiency, Lung dysfunction, or Kidney Yang depletion — fluids accumulate pathologically as dampness, edema, or [Phlegm](phlegm.md).

## Fluid pathology

**Fluid deficiency** (jin ye bu zu 津液不足): Insufficient fluids.
Dry skin, dry mouth, dry eyes, constipation, scanty concentrated urine, thirst.
Overlaps with [Yin deficiency](yin-deficiency.md) — Jin Ye are Yin substances, and their depletion is one expression of Yin depletion.

**Fluid accumulation**: When fluids are not transformed and excreted, they accumulate as: - **Dampness** (shi 湿) — diffuse, heavy, soggy - **[Phlegm](phlegm.md)** (tan 痰) — congealed, thick, obstructing - **Edema** (shui zhong 水肿) — visible fluid accumulation in tissues - **Fluid retention** (yin 饮) — fluid accumulation in body cavities

The progression — normal fluids → dampness → phlegm — represents increasing density and pathological severity of accumulated fluid.

## See also

- [Qi](qi.md) — moves and transforms body fluids
- [Blood (Xue)](xue.md) — the other major circulating fluid
- [Phlegm](phlegm.md) — the pathological product of impaired fluid metabolism
- [Yin Deficiency](yin-deficiency.md) — includes fluid depletion
- [Damp-Heat](damp-heat.md) — a pattern involving fluid accumulation with heat

records.name: Jing
records.description: The stored essence or constitutional substrate in TCM, encompassing inherited and acquired material reserves that underlie growth, reproduction, and aging

kaptchuk2000.title: The Web That Has No Weaver: Understanding Chinese Medicine

unschuld2003.title: Huang Di Nei Jing Su Wen: Nature, Knowledge, Imagery in an Ancient Chinese Medical Text

records.body:
Jing (精) is the first of the [Three Treasures](./san-bao.md) in [traditional Chinese medicine](traditional-chinese-medicine.md). It names the stored substrate — the material and constitutional basis from which the body's activity arises.

TCM distinguishes two aspects of Jing. Prenatal Jing (xian tian zhi jing 先天之精) is inherited from the parents and determines the body's constitutional foundation: its developmental trajectory, its resilience, its basic capacity. Postnatal Jing (hou tian zhi jing 後天之精) is acquired through food, breath, and rest — the ongoing material support that sustains the body's operations [@kaptchuk2000].

Jing is not identical to any single biomedical concept, though it overlaps with several. Constitutional predisposition, genetic inheritance, stored metabolic reserves, bone marrow, reproductive substance — all of these participate in what Jing names, but Jing is defined functionally rather than anatomically. It is what remains when activity ceases and what is drawn upon when activity resumes. In the *Huang Di Nei Jing*, Jing is associated with the Kidneys (as a functional system, not the anatomical organs) and with the deep reserves that govern growth, reproduction, and aging [@unschuld2003].

Jing depletes over a lifetime and replenishes slowly. Excessive labor, illness, and overexertion draw down Jing. Rest, nourishment, and moderation conserve it. The clinical signs of Jing depletion — premature aging, developmental delay, weakened bones, diminished reproductive capacity — describe a body whose substrate is thinning.

For information systems, Jing corresponds to persistent data and structural records: the stored substrate on which operational activity depends. A database is Jing. An archive is Jing. The accumulated schemas, records, and configurations that a system draws upon when it operates are its stored substrate. A system whose Jing is intact has the material to work with; whether it works well depends on [Qi](./qi.md) and [Shen](./shen.md).

## Related terms

- [Qi](./qi.md) — circulating energy, the operational layer
- [Shen](./shen.md) — reflective awareness, the capacity for adaptive response
- [San Bao](./san-bao.md) — the Three Treasures as a diagnostic system

records.name: Kidney
records.description: Shèn: the organ-function system of Chinese medicine that stores jing and so governs birth, growth, reproduction and ageing, rules water, and is the root of the body's yin and yang.

maciocia2015.title: The Foundations of Chinese Medicine: A Comprehensive Text

records.body:
The Kidney (腎, shèn) is one of the five yin organ-function systems of [zang-fu](./zang-fu.md) theory. It stores [jing](./jing.md), both the prenatal essence received at conception and the postnatal essence refined by the [Spleen](./spleen.md). Through jing it governs birth, growth, maturation, reproduction and the decline of ageing [@maciocia2015].

Kidney yin and Kidney yang are the root of the yin and yang of every other organ. Much long-standing illness is therefore read as ending in Kidney deficiency, and the conservation of jing, a traditional aim of [qigong](./qigong.md) and [neidan](./neidan.md), is conservation of the Kidney.

It produces marrow, which fills the brain and the bones. It governs water, and it "grasps" the qi the [Lung](./lung.md) sends down, which is why chronic breathlessness can be read as a Kidney pattern. It opens into the ears, shows in the head hair, houses the zhì (will), belongs to the water phase of [wu xing](./wu-xing.md), and is paired with the Bladder.

records.name: Liver
records.description: Gān: the organ-function system of Chinese medicine that stores blood and keeps qi flowing smoothly through the body and the emotions; its failure to do so, Liver qi stagnation, is among the commonest patterns.

maciocia2015.title: The Foundations of Chinese Medicine: A Comprehensive Text

records.body:
The Liver (肝, gān) is one of the five yin organ-function systems of [zang-fu](./zang-fu.md) theory. It stores [blood](./xue.md), releasing it to the muscles in activity and gathering it back at rest. It ensures the free, smooth flow of [qi](./qi.md) (shū xiè) through the whole body [@maciocia2015].

That smooth flow covers the emotions as well as the body. When it fails, the result is [qi stagnation](./qi-stagnation.md): distension and pain that move about, sighing, irritability, and in women premenstrual tension. It is one of the patterns [pattern diagnosis](./pattern-diagnosis.md) finds most often.

The Liver controls the sinews, opens into the eyes, shows in the nails, and houses the hún, the ethereal soul. It belongs to the wood phase of [wu xing](./wu-xing.md) and is paired with the Gall Bladder.

records.name: Long COVID
records.description: A chronic, multi-system condition following SARS-CoV-2 infection whose case definition varies substantially across the WHO clinical, RECOVER research, and NASEM disease-state frameworks, with prevalence estimates and mechanistic findings that must be read against which definition a given study used.

soriano2022.title: A clinical case definition of post-COVID-19 condition by a Delphi consensus

thaweethai2023.title: Development of a Definition of Postacute Sequelae of SARS-CoV-2 Infection

authors: National Academies of Sciences, Engineering, and Medicine
nasem2024.title: A Long COVID Definition: A Chronic, Systemic Disease State with Profound Consequences

records.body:
Long COVID is a chronic, often multi-system condition that follows SARS-CoV-2 infection, but it is not a single validated diagnostic entity — it is measured by at least three distinct instruments built for three different purposes, and a finding produced under one does not automatically transfer to the others. The WHO clinical case definition (Soriano et al., 2022, *Lancet Infectious Diseases* 22(4):e102-e107, doi:10.1016/S1473-3099(21)00703-9, PMID 34951953), reached by a two-round Delphi consensus of 265 patients, clinicians, researchers, and WHO staff, requires probable or confirmed SARS-CoV-2 infection, symptom onset usually within three months of that infection, symptoms lasting at least two months, and no alternative diagnosis that better explains them. The RECOVER research definition (Thaweethai et al., 2023, *JAMA* 329(22):1934-1946, doi:10.1001/jama.2023.8823, PMID 37278994) is a different instrument entirely: an empirically weighted composite score built from 12 of 44 screened symptoms — post-exertional malaise, fatigue, brain fog, dizziness, gastrointestinal symptoms, palpitations, changes in sexual desire or capacity, loss of or change in smell or taste, thirst, chronic cough, chest pain, and abnormal movements — assessed at six months or more post-infection in a cohort of 9,764 (8,646 infected, 1,118 uninfected controls), producing a research outcome variable rather than a clinical diagnosis. The 2024 NASEM definition (National Academies of Sciences, Engineering, and Medicine, *A Long COVID Definition: A Chronic, Systemic Disease State with Profound Consequences*, 2024) widens the frame again: an infection-associated chronic condition present at least three months as a continuous, relapsing-remitting, or progressive disease state affecting one or more organ systems, explicitly encompassing single-symptom presentations through to diagnosable conditions such as POTS, ME/CFS, interstitial lung disease, arrhythmias, diabetes, and autoimmune disorders.

Case-definition heterogeneity here is a research-validity issue, not a semantic quibble. The three definitions differ on the duration threshold (WHO: symptoms ≥2 months, onset ~3 months post-infection, so roughly a 5-month window; RECOVER: assessed at ≥6 months post-infection with no separate onset-timing requirement; NASEM: present at ≥3 months, with no upper bound and explicit allowance for relapsing-remitting or progressive courses rather than continuous persistence), on what counts as evidence (WHO and NASEM are consensus/expert-panel definitions; RECOVER is a data-derived symptom score fit to distinguish infected from uninfected participants), and on scope (WHO and RECOVER describe a symptom-based condition; NASEM explicitly subsumes other named diagnosable conditions, including ME/CFS, under its umbrella). A prevalence estimate, a mechanism study, or a treatment trial that does not state which of these it used cannot be safely pooled with one that used a different definition — the populations selected are measurably different, the same failure mode documented for ME/CFS case definitions (Fukuda vs. Canadian Consensus Criteria vs. IOM/SEID). This is precisely why prevalence estimates published on the subject range so widely: CDC Household Pulse Survey self-report puts current US adult prevalence around 6-7% (MMWR 72(32):866-870, 2023, PMID 37561665); the Global Burden of Disease Long COVID Collaborators' modeled estimate for three symptom clusters worldwide in 2020-2021 is 144.7 million with a 95% uncertainty interval of 54.8-312.9 million (Wulf Hanson et al., 2022, *JAMA* 328(16):1604-1615, doi:10.1001/jama.2022.18931, PMID 36215063); and a pooled meta-analysis of heterogeneous, mostly uncontrolled studies reported 45% of survivors symptomatic at roughly four months (O'Mahoney et al., 2023, *eClinicalMedicine* 55:101762, PMID 36474804), a figure that drew published methodological criticism in the same journal for pooling across inconsistent symptom-duration thresholds and lacking uninfected comparators in most included studies. None of these three numbers is wrong on its own terms; none is directly comparable to either of the others.

## Core symptom clusters

Across the three definitional frameworks, the symptom domains that recur most consistently in both consensus definitions and empirically derived symptom scores are: **fatigue** and **post-exertional malaise** (worsening of symptoms after physical, cognitive, or emotional exertion); **cognitive dysfunction** ("brain fog," memory and concentration difficulty); **respiratory symptoms** (dyspnea, chronic cough); **cardiovascular/autonomic symptoms** (palpitations, orthostatic intolerance, and diagnosable POTS in a subset of patients); **gastrointestinal symptoms**; and **sensory changes** (altered or lost smell or taste). The Global Burden of Disease modeling work organizes the condition around three of these clusters specifically (fatigue, cognitive, respiratory) as the clusters with the strongest cross-cohort evidence base; the RECOVER composite score adds palpitations, thirst, chest pain, sexual-function changes, and abnormal movements as further symptoms found to statistically distinguish infected from uninfected participants at six months. Post-exertional malaise recurs as a symptom shared with myalgic encephalomyelitis, and a subset of long COVID patients meet ME/CFS case criteria outright — the NASEM definition names this overlap explicitly rather than treating the two as unrelated. No consensus symptom list is exhaustive or universal across patients; long COVID is understood as mechanistically and phenotypically heterogeneous, and subtype identification (which symptom clusters co-occur, and by which mechanism) remains active research rather than a settled taxonomy.

## Related terms

- Myalgic encephalomyelitis — the condition a subset of long COVID patients meet case criteria for, sharing post-exertional malaise as a cardinal feature and a structurally similar case-definition-heterogeneity problem
- Postural orthostatic tachycardia syndrome — the most frequently reported specific autonomic diagnosis among long COVID patients with dysautonomia
- Post-exertional malaise — the symptom retained in the RECOVER composite score and shared with myalgic encephalomyelitis
- Central sensitization — a contrasting mechanistic frame (peripheral/central pain amplification) relevant to distinguishing long COVID's pain and cognitive symptoms from other chronic-pain mechanisms

records.name: Lorazepam challenge test
records.description: A diagnostic-and-therapeutic probe in which parenteral lorazepam is given to a patient with suspected catatonia and the rated response is used both to support the diagnosis and to predict response to a full lorazepam treatment trial.

bush1996b.title: Catatonia. II. Treatment with lorazepam and electroconvulsive therapy

leroy2018.title: Is electroconvulsive therapy an evidence-based treatment for catatonia? A systematic review and meta-analysis
leroy2018.publication: European Archives of Psychiatry and Clinical Neuroscience

records.body:
The lorazepam challenge test is a diagnostic-and-therapeutic probe for catatonia: an initial parenteral (typically intravenous) dose of lorazepam is given to a patient with suspected catatonic signs, and the response — commonly rated with an instrument such as the Bush-Francis Catatonia Rating Scale — is used both to support the diagnosis and to gauge whether a full lorazepam treatment trial is likely to succeed. In the study that formalized this practice, 28 catatonic patients were treated with parenteral and/or oral lorazepam for up to five days, 11 of them receiving an initial intravenous lorazepam challenge before the extended trial.

The challenge test is distinct from the full lorazepam treatment trial that may follow it: the challenge is a single dose used as a rapid diagnostic and prognostic probe, while the trial is the sustained course used to try to resolve catatonic signs. A positive response to the initial parenteral challenge predicted eventual response to the full lorazepam trial, as did a shorter duration of catatonic symptoms before treatment began — meaning the challenge's value is specifically prognostic, indicating who is likely to respond to a lorazepam trial, not merely confirmatory of the catatonia diagnosis in isolation.

Of 21 patients who completed a full lorazepam trial, 16 (76%) had resolution of catatonic signs, and of those who failed lorazepam, electroconvulsive therapy produced a prompt response in all 4 who received it — establishing lorazepam as an effective first-line approach with electroconvulsive therapy as an effective second-line option for nonresponders in this systematically treated sample. A separate systematic review and meta-analysis of electroconvulsive therapy for catatonia — 564 patients across 28 studies, 10 poolable for pre-post comparison — found a very large pooled improvement (standardized mean difference -3.14, 95% CI -3.95 to -2.34) but concluded that, because the identified randomized trials were low-quality and heterogeneous, the literature "fails to demonstrate efficacy and effectiveness" by rigorous trial standards despite consistently describing improvement — a large observational effect without an equivalent randomized-trial-grade demonstration. Neither study stratifies response by pole: the 76% response figure and the electroconvulsive-therapy effect size describe treated catatonia broadly, not whether the retarded or excited pole responds better, and neither figure should be generalized as a population base rate for catatonia response outside similarly sized, systematically treated inpatient samples.

## Related terms

- Catatonia — the syndrome this test diagnoses and treats
- Bush-Francis catatonia rating scale — the instrument commonly used to rate response to the challenge

records.name: Lung
records.description: Fèi: the organ-function system of Chinese medicine that governs qi and breathing, spreads defensive qi and fluids to the surface and moves them downward, and rules the skin; the uppermost and most exposed of the yin organs.

maciocia2015.title: The Foundations of Chinese Medicine: A Comprehensive Text

records.body:
The Lung (肺, fèi) is one of the five yin organ-function systems of [zang-fu](./zang-fu.md) theory. Like every zang it names a set of functions, which overlap with but are not identical to the anatomical lungs.

It governs [qi](./qi.md) and respiration. Breathing draws in the "clear qi" of the air, which combines with the food essence sent up by the [Spleen](./spleen.md) to form the gathering qi (zōng qì) of the chest. Its movements are twofold [@maciocia2015]:
- **Spreading** (xuān fā): it disperses [defensive qi](./wei-qi.md) and fluids to the surface, where they warm the skin and guard against external pathogens.
- **Descending** (sù jiàng): it sends qi and fluids downward, toward the Kidney and the lower body, and so is said to regulate the water passages.

Because it spreads defensive qi to the surface, the Lung rules the skin and body hair. It opens into the nose, belongs to the metal phase of [wu xing](./wu-xing.md), is paired with the Large Intestine, and houses the pò, the corporeal soul. As the uppermost organ, the first to meet wind and cold, it is called the "delicate organ".

In [pattern diagnosis](./pattern-diagnosis.md), a cough, shortness of breath, a weak voice, catching colds easily and sweating on slight exertion are read as Lung qi deficiency. The breath-centred practices of [qigong](./qigong.md), [Liuzijue](./liuzijue.md) above all, are traditionally prescribed to strengthen it.

records.name: Malignant catatonia
records.description: A hyperthermic, autonomically unstable, severely rigid variant of catatonia carrying substantial risk of death if untreated, clinically difficult to separate from neuroleptic malignant syndrome and, by some accounts, not categorically distinct from it.

philbrick1994.title: Malignant catatonia
philbrick1994.publication: Journal of Neuropsychiatry and Clinical Neurosciences

records.body:
Malignant catatonia is a severe variant of the catatonic syndrome marked by hyperthermia, autonomic instability, and severe rigidity, historically described in the world literature as "lethal catatonia" because of its substantial risk of death if untreated. A 1986 world-literature review characterized it as "a syndrome rather than a specific disease," arising from both functional psychiatric illness and organic (general-medical or neurological) disease, and reported that its prevalence appeared to have declined with modern psychopharmacologic treatment while cases continued to occur.

Malignant catatonia is clinically difficult to separate from neuroleptic malignant syndrome (NMS), the rigidity-and-hyperthermia syndrome associated with antipsychotic exposure, and the relationship between the two is contested rather than settled: a 1994 review proposing a revised malignant/nonmalignant catatonia nomenclature argued that malignant catatonia has causes beyond neuroleptic exposure, meaning NMS is one route into a broader malignant-catatonia picture rather than a categorically separate illness. Clinical reviews consistently describe a differential pattern — malignant catatonia tending to show waxy flexibility and catalepsy together with a preceding prodrome of excitement or agitation before rigidity sets in, versus NMS classically beginning with "lead-pipe" rigidity without such a prodrome, tied temporally to antipsychotic exposure — but no single primary study establishing this differential with reported sensitivity or specificity was located; it is best treated as clinical teaching rather than a validated discriminating instrument.

The consequence for clinical observation and research design is twofold. Quantified mortality figures for malignant catatonia circulate widely in secondary teaching, but the primary 1986 world-literature review itself reports no quantified mortality percentage, so any specific mortality figure asserted for malignant catatonia should be treated as unverified against that primary source rather than repeated as established fact. And because the excitement-before-rigidity prodrome pattern is descriptive teaching rather than a quantified, prospectively validated finding, establishing it as a genuine discriminator from NMS would require a head-to-head comparison with defined sensitivity and specificity — not yet available in the literature reviewed here — before the pattern can be used as a diagnostic instrument rather than a clinical impression.

## Related terms

- Catatonia — the broader syndrome of which this is the hyperthermic, high-mortality-risk variant
- Waxy flexibility — one of the signs whose presence, alongside catalepsy, features in the clinical differential from neuroleptic malignant syndrome
- Bush-Francis catatonia rating scale — the instrument used to rate severity and track treatment response

records.name: Mast cell
records.description: A tissue-resident granulocyte stationed at barrier surfaces and around vessels and nerves, storing preformed mediators for release within seconds of activation by IgE-dependent or IgE-independent triggers including neuropeptides and adrenergic signals.

galli2020.title: Mast Cells in Inflammation and Disease: Recent Progress and Ongoing Concerns
galli2020.note: PMID 32340580; resolved against CrossRef and PubMed 2026-09-02

records.body:
A mast cell is a tissue-resident granulocyte, seated at barrier surfaces and around blood vessels and peripheral nerves, that stores preformed mediators including histamine and tryptase in granules and releases them within seconds of activation [galli2020]. Activation is classically IgE-dependent through the high-affinity IgE receptor, but IgE-independent routes — including complement fragments, neuropeptides, and drugs acting at MRGPRX2 — are established, which is the **acts-through** relation to receptor asserted here.

Unlike circulating leukocytes recruited to a site after injury, it is already stationed in the tissue and can act before any recruitment occurs, which makes it an immediate rather than a recruited effector. **Established.**

Its position beside vessels and nerves means an activation event couples the immune, vascular, and sensory systems in one step, so a mast-cell mediated symptom cannot be assigned to any one of those systems on its own. Galli, Gaudenzio and Tsai's review states the ongoing concern directly: the cell's roles are established in allergic disease and host defence, while its proposed contributions to many other conditions rest on weaker evidence [galli2020]. **A note on the infection-associated chronic illness literature specifically**: mast-cell involvement in myalgic encephalomyelitis is a proposed mechanism, not an established finding — a targeted PubMed search on 2026-09-02 for mast-cell activation in that population returned clinical-overlap discussion and one small open treatment report, and no controlled demonstration of degranulation in a diagnosed cohort.

records.name: Mast Cell Degranulation
records.description: The release of preformed and newly synthesized mediators (histamine, tryptase, prostaglandins, leukotrienes) from tissue-resident mast cells, triggered by IgE-dependent and IgE-independent mechanisms including adrenergic signalling and neuropeptides.
records.body:
Mast cells are tissue-resident granulocytes distributed throughout the body at barrier surfaces (skin, gut, respiratory tract) and in neural-rich tissues. Their granules contain preformed mediators — histamine, tryptase, heparin, and other proteases — that are released rapidly when the cell is triggered, along with newly synthesized lipid mediators (prostaglandins and leukotrienes) generated within minutes of activation. Degranulation is the exocytotic discharge of these granules into the extracellular space, where the mediators act on local tissues and vasculature to produce immediate vascular permeability, smooth-muscle contraction, and pain. The classical understanding emphasizes IgE-dependent triggering: cross-linking of IgE molecules bound to high-affinity FcεRI receptors on the mast cell surface recruits Lyn and Syk kinases to the receptor, activating downstream phospholipase-C and calcium signalling, resulting in rapid degranulation. This is the pathway that dominates acute allergic reactions, where allergen-specific IgE on mast cells is cross-linked by allergen.

The IgE-independent pathways are equally important and are often underemphasized in standard accounts. Mast cells express MRGPRX2, a G-protein-coupled receptor activated by certain neuropeptides (substance P, calcitonin-gene-related peptide, neuropeptide Y), bacterial lipopolysaccharides, and various drugs (opioids, antibiotics), which triggers degranulation independently of IgE. The adrenergic nervous system can also trigger mast cell degranulation via β2-adrenergic receptor signalling and, under stress conditions involving norepinephrine surges, can mobilize mast cell mediators without any involvement of allergen or antibody. Complement (C5a and C3a) can directly activate mast cells through C3aR and C5aR receptors. These IgE-independent routes are mechanistically critical for understanding mast cell involvement in stress-related physiology, since a sympathetic surge can trigger central and peripheral mast cell degranulation without requiring prior IgE sensitization to an allergen.

Mast cell degranulation must be distinguished from mast cell activation syndrome (MCAS) as a clinical diagnosis. MCAS is a clinical entity characterized by recurrent symptoms attributed to mast cell-driven mediator release, typically involving flushing, urticaria, angioedema, gastrointestinal symptoms, and cardiovascular instability. However, diagnostic criteria for MCAS are genuinely contested: criteria vary between proposed schemas (WHO, international consensus proposals from 2012 onwards), and confirmation of a diagnosis typically requires serum tryptase levels sampled within the symptom episode (usually a matter of minutes to hours after symptom onset) compared against a personal baseline — a practically difficult requirement. Moreover, the diagnosis of MCAS in the absence of documented elevated tryptase remains controversial, since tryptase elevation is inconsistent across symptomatic episodes, and basal serum tryptase itself varies widely between individuals. The proposed involvement of mast cell degranulation in ME/CFS is a hypothesis with limited direct evidence: some ME/CFS patients report flushing, urticaria, and gastrointestinal symptoms superficially compatible with mast cell release, and small case series have documented elevated tryptase in some individuals, but systematic prospective studies correlating MCAS diagnostic criteria with ME/CFS diagnosis and with cytokine or symptom patterns are lacking.

The practical consequence of the degranulation mechanism is that tryptase, the most commonly measured mast cell mediator, is only detectable in serum at levels above baseline for a narrow window around the time of degranulation — typically a few hours. A blood sample must be drawn within hours of a suspected mast cell degranulation episode, and compared against that individual's own personal baseline tryptase level (measured at a quiescent time), to establish whether an elevation has occurred. Histamine is even more transient, with half-life measured in minutes, making it essentially impossible to measure retrospectively. This timing requirement means that establishing whether a particular clinical episode involved mast cell degranulation depends entirely on having drawn a timed blood sample during the event — a demand that makes epidemiological or clinical research on mast cell involvement in poorly-characterized conditions (such as ME/CFS) extraordinarily difficult, and explains why mast cell-mediator data in such conditions remain sparse.

## Related terms

- Histamine — a key preformed mediator released by mast cells
- Neuropeptide — one class of trigger for IgE-independent mast cell activation
- Immunity — the broader immune system of which mast cells are one component
- Inflammation — the local tissue consequence of mast cell degranulation

records.name: Airway
records.body:
The anatomical passage carrying gas between the environment and the lungs, assessed clinically through four functions: patency, oxygenation, ventilation, and protection.

The **airway** is the anatomical passage that carries gas between the environment and the lungs. In clinical practice it is divided into upper and lower segments, a distinction that organizes both assessment and intervention.

The **upper airway** extends from the nose and mouth through the pharynx (nasopharynx, oropharynx, hypopharynx) to the larynx and vocal cords. It is responsible for filtering, warming, and humidifying inspired air and for protecting the lower airway from aspiration. Upper-airway problems tend to produce [stridor](../../../../services/airway-services-section/content/text/glossary/terms/stridor.md) — a high-pitched inspiratory sound indicating narrowing above or at the level of the vocal cords.

The **lower airway** extends from the trachea through the bronchi and bronchioles to the alveoli, where gas exchange occurs. Lower-airway problems tend to produce [wheeze](../../../../services/airway-services-section/content/text/glossary/terms/wheeze.md) — a musical expiratory sound indicating narrowing below the vocal cords, typically from bronchospasm or mucus plugging.

The clinical significance of the airway is defined by four bedside functions:

- **Patency** — Is the passage open? Obstruction at any level threatens all downstream functions.

- **[Oxygenation](../../../../services/airway-services-section/content/text/glossary/terms/oxygenation.md)** — Is oxygen reaching arterial blood?

- **[Ventilation](../../../../services/airway-services-section/content/text/glossary/terms/ventilation.md)** — Is carbon dioxide being eliminated?

- **Protection** — Is the airway defended against aspiration of gastric contents, blood, or secretions?

Each function can fail independently. A patient can have a patent airway but inadequate oxygenation (as in pneumonia). A patient can be well-oxygenated but poorly ventilated (as in early opioid toxicity, where supplemental oxygen may mask rising CO2). Assessing all four functions — not just one — is the foundation of airway management.

records.name: Cannot-Intubate, Cannot-Oxygenate (CICO)
records.body:
A critical airway emergency in which both tracheal intubation and noninvasive oxygenation have failed, requiring immediate surgical airway rescue.

Requires

- cricothyrotomy
- preoxygenation

**Cannot-Intubate, Cannot-Oxygenate (CICO)** is a critical airway emergency in which both tracheal intubation and [oxygenation](../../../../services/airway-services-section/content/text/glossary/terms/oxygenation.md) by noninvasive methods have failed. It is the most dangerous situation in airway management and requires immediate activation of a surgical rescue pathway.

CICO is defined by two simultaneous failures:

- **Cannot intubate** — direct or video laryngoscopy has failed to achieve tracheal intubation, and a [supraglottic airway](../../../../services/airway-services-section/content/text/glossary/terms/supraglottic-airway.md) either cannot be placed or does not provide adequate ventilation

- **Cannot oxygenate** — bag-mask ventilation is ineffective and the patient’s oxygen saturation is falling despite all noninvasive efforts

When both conditions are met, the patient will die of hypoxia unless a surgical airway is established. The rescue procedure is emergency cricothyrotomy — creating an opening through the cricothyroid membrane (between the thyroid and cricoid cartilages) to bypass the obstructed upper airway and provide direct access to the trachea.

CICO is rare. In elective anesthesia, the incidence is estimated at roughly 1 in 50,000 cases. But its rarity is part of what makes it dangerous: most clinicians will encounter it only once or twice in a career, which means the response must be trained and rehearsed rather than learned through experience.

The factors that contribute to CICO emergencies include:

- **Unanticipated difficult airway** — anatomy that was not predicted to be difficult but proves resistant to intubation

- **Progressive airway obstruction** — angioedema, expanding hematoma, or airway burns that worsen during management attempts

- **Failed escalation** — each step in the airway management ladder (bag-mask, SGA, intubation) fails in sequence, consuming time and oxygen reserves

- **Inadequate [preoxygenation](../../../../services/airway-services-section/content/text/glossary/terms/preoxygenation.md)** — a patient who enters the intubation attempt with low oxygen reserves reaches critical desaturation faster, compressing the time available for rescue
