- [Emodin](emodin.md) — another major bioactive compound from the same plant
- [Japanese Knotweed as Medicine](../../../../../herbalism-services-section/content/text/documents/articles/notes/japanese-knotweed-as-medicine.md) — comprehensive medicinal text

records.name: Retarded catatonia
records.description: The hypokinetic pole of catatonia — stupor, immobility, mutism, and waxy flexibility — distinguished from the excited pole by the direction of the motor abnormality, not by the presence or absence of catatonic signs. No primary study locates or measures the transition between this pole and the excited pole.

dawkins2022.title: Catatonia Psychopathology and Phenomenology in a Large Dataset

goldar1995.title: Karl Ludwig Kahlbaum's concept of catatonia

records.body:
Retarded catatonia — also called stuporous or akinetic catatonia — names the hypokinetic pole of the catatonic syndrome: profound psychomotor slowing or arrest expressed as stupor, immobility, mutism, and waxy flexibility (a limb or posture that yields to passive repositioning and is then held in place). It is not a separately coded DSM-5-TR diagnosis; a patient meeting the syndrome's three-of-twelve-sign threshold predominantly through these hypokinetic signs and a patient meeting the identical threshold predominantly through hyperkinetic signs both receive the same diagnosis of catatonia, differentiated informally by clinicians as the retarded and excited poles.

The retarded and excited poles are distinguished by the direction of the motor abnormality, not by the presence or absence of catatonic signs: both draw on the same twelve-item sign list and the same diagnostic threshold, and often occur in the same patient. In a retrospective cohort of 1,456 patients across 2,130 catatonic episodes, 925 patients showed stupor/immobility, and of those, 105 (11.4%) also showed excitement within the same episode — a minority, but real overlap that the study's authors interpret as "alternation" between poles within one syndrome rather than two mutually exclusive subtypes. Kahlbaum's original 1874 description already framed catatonia this way, as a syndrome running a cyclic, alternating course through melancholic (retarded) and manic (excited) phases in the same patients, rather than as one static hypokinetic entity.

No primary study located in the literature reviewed for this term measures the transition between the retarded and excited poles directly: no imaging, receptor-binding, or biomarker study scans a patient during a retarded-to-excited switch, and the strongest available transition-relevant evidence — the 1,456-patient cohort above — is a cross-sectional, record-coded co-occurrence analysis, not a prospective or moment-to-moment observation of switching. It establishes that stupor and excitement can coexist within an episode, not the direction, speed, or trigger of a change from one to the other. The consequence for observation is that a single-timepoint rating cannot establish whether, or how, a given patient is moving between poles; only repeated ratings across the course of an episode could address that question, and none of the located literature reports having done so.

## Related terms

- Catatonia — the syndrome of which this is one motor pole
- Excited catatonia — the hyperkinetic pole, which co-occurs with this pole in a minority of patients
- Waxy flexibility — one of the hallmark signs of this pole
- Bush-Francis catatonia rating scale — the instrument used to rate hypokinetic and hyperkinetic signs alike

records.name: San Bao (Three Treasures)
records.description: The diagnostic framework of Jing, Qi, and Shen — three layered aspects of vitality used in TCM and Daoist practice to assess the health of a living system

kaptchuk2000.title: The Web That Has No Weaver

records.body:
The San Bao (三寶), the Three Treasures, are [Jing](./jing.md) (essence), [Qi](./qi.md) (vital energy), and [Shen](./shen.md) (spirit).
Together they form a diagnostic framework for describing layers of vitality in a living system.

The framework is shared between [traditional Chinese medicine](traditional-chinese-medicine.md) and Daoist cultivational practice, though each tradition emphasizes different aspects [@schipper1993; @kohn2000].
In TCM, the Three Treasures organize clinical assessment: a practitioner evaluates whether the patient's substrate is intact (Jing), whether their functional activities are proceeding (Qi), and whether their engagement with the world is coherent and responsive (Shen).
In Daoist practice, cultivating the Three Treasures — conserving Jing, circulating Qi, refining Shen — is the path toward integrated vitality.

The three are not independent substances.
They are three aspects of a single living process, distinguished by their level of refinement:

| Treasure | Character | Layer | Diagnostic question |
|---|---|---|---|
| Jing | 精 | Stored substrate | Does the system have material to work with? |
| Qi | 氣 | Circulating activity | Are the system's operations proceeding? |
| Shen | 神 | Reflective awareness | Is the system responsive to its situation? |

The dependencies run upward.
Qi draws on Jing: without a substrate, there are no operations to sustain.
Shen depends on Qi: without operational activity, there is nothing to be aware of.
But the relationship is not additive.
More Jing does not automatically produce more Qi, and more Qi does not automatically produce more Shen.
Each layer has its own conditions for health and its own modes of failure [@kaptchuk2000].

This layered structure is what makes the framework diagnostically useful.
A system can fail at any layer independently:

- **Jing depleted, Qi and Shen present**: the system is aware and active but running out of material.
  A researcher who is intellectually sharp but physically exhausted.
  A database approaching storage limits while its query engine runs smoothly.
- **Qi stagnant, Jing and Shen present**: the system has substrate and awareness but its operations are blocked.
  A person with full reserves but functional paralysis.
  A well-stocked archive whose search infrastructure has failed.
- **Shen absent, Jing and Qi present**: the system has substrate and operational activity but no reflective capacity.
  The body moves but does not adapt.
  The data circulates but the system cannot question whether its own categories still serve.

The third condition — Qi without Shen — is the one that has no standard name in Western systems vocabulary.
The system is not broken.
It is not inert.
It operates, often vigorously.
But it operates within frames it cannot examine.
It corrects errors but does not question whether the reference state is still appropriate.
In [cybernetic terms](../../information/terms/cybernetics.md), it performs [single-loop learning](../../../../../../../../../information-science-services-section/services/cybernetics-services-section/content/text/glossary/terms/single-loop-double-loop-learning.md) without [double-loop learning](../../../../../../../../../information-science-services-section/services/cybernetics-services-section/content/text/glossary/terms/single-loop-double-loop-learning.md).
In Daoist folklore, this condition has a figure: the jiangshi (僵尸), the hopping corpse — animated by residual Qi, joints locked, unable to adapt its movement to the situation.

The Three Treasures framework does not rank Shen above Qi or Qi above Jing.
A system needs all three.
An abundance of Shen without adequate Qi is awareness without the operational capacity to act on what it perceives.
The diagnostic value is in identifying which layer is compromised, not in asserting that one layer matters more than the others.

## Related terms

- [Jing](./jing.md) — the first treasure, stored substrate
- [Qi](./qi.md) — the second treasure, circulating energy
- [Shen](./shen.md) — the third treasure, reflective awareness
- [Traditional Chinese Medicine](traditional-chinese-medicine.md) — the medical tradition that uses this framework
- [Single-loop and double-loop learning](../../../../../../../../../information-science-services-section/services/cybernetics-services-section/content/text/glossary/terms/single-loop-double-loop-learning.md) — the Western vocabulary closest to the Qi/Shen distinction
- [Second-order cybernetics](../../../../../../../../../../../information-science-services-section/services/cybernetics-services-section/content/text/glossary/terms/second-order-cybernetics.md) — reflexive observation as a capacity distinct from first-order operation

records.name: san jiao
records.description: 三焦 — the Triple Burner, a Fu organ defined functionally as the pathway of water, grain, and Qi through the upper, middle, and lower body cavities, with no fixed anatomical structure of its own
records.body:
San Jiao (三焦), the Triple Burner or Triple Energizer, is one of the six Fu organs of Traditional Chinese Medicine and the clearest instance in the entire Zang-Fu system of an organ defined purely by function, with no anatomical structure that corresponds to it. It divides the trunk into three functional regions — upper, middle, and lower burner — and governs the movement of Qi and the passage of fluids between them.

## Classical basis

The primary classical source for San Jiao's definition is the *Nan Jing* (《難經》), Difficulty 31 (三十一難), which poses the question directly — "三焦者，何稟何生？何始何終？其治常在何許？可曉以不？" (the Triple Burner — from what does it receive its charge, from what is it born, where does it begin and end, where is its seat of treatment?) — and answers: "三焦者，水穀之道路，氣之所終始也" (the Triple Burner is the pathway of water and grain, the place where Qi begins and ends). The same passage assigns distinct functions and locations to each division: the upper burner (上焦), below the heart and above the diaphragm, at the opening of the stomach, "governs intake without outflow"; the middle burner (中焦), at the middle cavity of the stomach, "neither above nor below," governs the ripening and decomposition of water and grain; the lower burner (下焦), at the upper opening of the bladder, governs the separation of clear from turbid and outflow without intake. Later commentary summarized San Jiao's defining paradox as 有名無形 — "named, but without form" — a phrase associated with this doctrine even where it does not appear verbatim in Difficulty 31 itself.

## The three burners

**Upper Burner (上焦)**: Encompasses the Heart and Lung, above the diaphragm. Governs respiration and the circulation of Qi and Blood to the whole body; its characteristic description is "like a mist" (如霧), diffusing nourishment outward and upward.

**Middle Burner (中焦)**: Encompasses the Spleen and Stomach, between diaphragm and navel. Governs the digestion, transformation, and transportation of food and drink (Yun Hua); its characteristic description is "like a maceration vat" (如漚), fermenting and ripening ingested material into usable essence.

**Lower Burner (下焦)**: Encompasses the Kidney, Bladder, and Large and Small Intestine, below the navel. Governs the separation of the clear from the turbid and the elimination of waste; its characteristic description is "like a drainage ditch" (如瀆), directing what is no longer needed downward and out.

## Function as a whole

Beyond the three regional descriptions, San Jiao as a single organ is credited with governing the free flow of Qi throughout the entire body and, distinctively among the Fu organs, with governing the pathways (水道) through which fluids move — a function it shares closely with the Lung, Spleen, and Kidney, the three organs classically credited with fluid metabolism. San Jiao is paired, in the twelve-meridian system, with the Pericardium, and some classical sources count the Pericardium as a sixth Zang organ specifically to preserve the six-pair structure that San Jiao's inclusion would otherwise leave unbalanced.

## Clinical significance

Because San Jiao has no dedicated pathology of its own separable from the organs it contains, clinical use of the concept is largely diagnostic and organizational rather than a target of treatment in isolation. "Damp-Heat obstructing the Triple Burner" describes a pattern in which dampness and heat block the free passage of fluid and Qi through all three regions at once, producing a diffuse presentation — chest oppression, epigastric fullness, and lower-body heaviness together — that would otherwise have to be described as three separate regional problems. San Jiao's diagnostic value lies precisely in offering a single frame for conditions that span the whole trunk rather than settling in one organ.

## Biomedical convergence, honestly graded

San Jiao has attracted more speculative biomedical mapping than almost any other TCM concept precisely because it has no anatomical referent to test against directly — proposals have included the mesentery, the fascial planes of the body cavity, the lymphatic system, and the interstitium (the fluid-filled connective tissue network described in recent anatomical literature). None of these proposals has achieved anything close to consensus, and San Jiao's own classical definition (有名無形, "named but without form") should be read as a functional classification of processes — respiration and circulation above, digestion in the middle, elimination below, and fluid passage throughout — rather than a placeholder anatomical structure awaiting biomedical discovery. The honest position is that San Jiao is doing organizational work TCM's diagnostic system needs (grouping the trunk's Qi and fluid dynamics into one coherent picture) and that no biomedical structure has been shown to do the same organizational work; treating a specific candidate structure as San Jiao's "real" referent would overstate what the comparison supports.

records.name: San Tiao
records.description: The three regulations of qigong: regulating the body (posture and movement), the breath, and the mind (attention and intent), practised together as one act.
records.body:
San tiao (三調), the three regulations, is how modern teaching of [qigong](./qigong.md) states what every form has in common:

- **Regulating the body** (tiáo shēn, 調身): posture, alignment, and relaxation in stillness, and the path and rhythm of each movement in motion.
- **Regulating the breath** (tiáo xī, 調息): the breath is first allowed to be natural, then made slow, even, fine, and long, usually abdominal. Some methods coordinate it with movement or add sounds; Liuzijue, for example, pairs six exhaled sounds with the organ-function systems.
- **Regulating the mind** (tiáo xīn, 調心): attention is gathered, often in the lower [dantian](./dantian.md), and intent (yì) accompanies the movement instead of wandering.

The three are not steps done in order. A practice counts as qigong, not as calisthenics, breathing drill, or meditation, when the three are regulated together. Chinese texts describe the goal as the three merging into one (sān tiáo hé yī).

The formulation is a twentieth-century systematization from the clinics that built modern qigong. Older daoyin and neidan texts speak of the same elements in their own vocabularies. Because it names the components an intervention combines, it is also a useful frame for research. A trial that compares a form with ordinary exercise or with breathing alone is asking which of the three regulations carries the effect.

records.name: Self/Non-Self Discrimination
records.description: The immune system's foundational classification problem: distinguishing the body's own molecular constituents from foreign material, established during lymphocyte development and maintained through ongoing tolerance mechanisms.
records.body:
Self/non-self discrimination is the classical framework for how the adaptive immune system decides what to attack. Frank Macfarlane Burnet's clonal selection theory (1957) held that the immune system pre-generates an enormous repertoire of lymphocytes bearing randomly assorted antigen receptors, then eliminates or inactivates those clones whose receptors bind the body's own molecules — leaving a surviving repertoire tuned to recognize only what is foreign.

## Establishing the boundary

The boundary is set during lymphocyte development, not inherited as a fixed list:

- **Central tolerance** — in the thymus, developing T cells are tested against self-antigens displayed by thymic epithelial and dendritic cells. Cells that bind self-antigens too strongly undergo negative selection (apoptosis); cells that fail to bind at all also die (positive selection requires some self-recognition, just not too much). Only cells in the narrow window — weak self-affinity — survive to leave the thymus. A parallel process (central B cell tolerance) occurs in the bone marrow.
- **Peripheral tolerance** — self-reactive lymphocytes that escape central deletion are held in check by regulatory T cells, anergy (functional inactivation on encountering antigen without costimulation), and clonal ignorance (antigens sequestered from immune surveillance, as in the eye or testis).

The boundary set this way is not permanent — it is a repertoire configuration reached through a developmental process and then actively maintained. See [immunological tolerance](./immunological-tolerance.md) for the maintenance mechanisms and [autoimmunity](./autoimmunity.md) for what happens when they fail.

## Limits of the framework

Self/non-self discrimination struggles to explain several observations without amendment: why the immune system tolerates the fetus (paternal antigens are non-self, yet pregnancy does not trigger rejection under normal conditions), why it tolerates commensal gut microbiota in enormous non-self quantities, and why transplanted tissue is rejected only under some conditions and not others. Polly Matzinger's [danger model](./danger-model.md) (1994) was proposed partly to address these gaps by keying immune response to signals of tissue damage rather than to foreignness per se.

## A framing from outside immunology

The founding note for this section's theory arc reads self/non-self discrimination as a case of a more general pattern — a system reaching a settled classification over a domain of possible inputs before it is asked to act on any particular one. See ["Immunity as Belief Board"](../../../../../../../../../../../../content/text/documents/articles/notes/2026/08/21/2026-08-21-note-on-immunity-as-belief-board.md), which frames thymic negative selection as "a charge configuration over the antigen space reaching its fixed point before deployment." That note is a draft awaiting the section's owner review; its claims are presented there as a hypothesis to be tested, not settled immunology, and this section is a candidate destination for it rather than an endorsement of it.

## Related terms

- [Immunological tolerance](./immunological-tolerance.md) — how the boundary is maintained after it is set
- [Autoimmunity](./autoimmunity.md) — what happens when self/non-self classification misfires
- [Danger model](./danger-model.md) — an alternative to keying response on self/non-self at all
- [Idiotypic network](./idiotypic-network.md) — a theory of how the repertoire is organized relative to itself, not only to antigen

records.name: Sham Stimulation
records.description: A control condition in device trials that mimics the look, set-up and, ideally, the feel of real stimulation while delivering no active dose, so that the device's specific effect can be separated from expectation.

bikson2016.title: Safety of transcranial direct current stimulation: evidence based update 2016

records.body:
In a device trial the sham is the placebo: the same headset, electrodes, session length and ritual, but no effective stimulation. A good sham is indistinguishable from the real thing to the participant, and ideally to the staff as well.

That is hard for anything that can be felt. In [tDCS](../../../../services/medical-technology-services-section/services/electrotherapy-devices-services-section/content/text/glossary/terms/transcranial-direct-current-stimulation.md) the usual sham ramps the current up for 30 seconds to produce the tingle, then switches it off. Experienced participants can often tell [@bikson2016]. [Cranial electrotherapy](../../../../services/medical-technology-services-section/services/electrotherapy-devices-services-section/content/text/glossary/terms/cranial-electrotherapy-stimulation.md) devices that run below the threshold of sensation have the opposite property: the sham is truly indistinguishable, but there is then no way to confirm the active device was delivering anything noticeable either. How well a sham works determines how far [placebo effects](placebo-effect.md) can be separated from the device's own action, which is why good trials check whether participants could guess their group.

records.name: Shen
records.description: The capacity for awareness, responsiveness, and coherent engagement with novelty — the third of the Three Treasures, assessed clinically through the patient's eyes, bearing, and affect

kaptchuk2000.title: The Web That Has No Weaver

unschuld2003.title: Huang Di Nei Jing Su Wen: Nature, Knowledge, Imagery in an Ancient Chinese Medical Text

records.body:
Shen (神) is the third of the [Three Treasures](./san-bao.md) in [traditional Chinese medicine](traditional-chinese-medicine.md).
It names the capacity for awareness, responsiveness, and coherent engagement with novelty.

Shen is often translated as "spirit" or "mind," but neither translation captures the concept's clinical specificity.
In TCM diagnosis, Shen is what a practitioner assesses when they observe the patient's eyes, complexion, bearing, and responsiveness.
Bright eyes, a clear complexion, coherent speech, and appropriate emotional responses indicate that Shen is present.
Dull eyes, a waxy complexion, confused speech, and flattened or inappropriate affect indicate that Shen is disturbed or absent [@kaptchuk2000].

This makes Shen a diagnostic category, not a metaphysical claim.
The practitioner is not asserting the existence of a soul.
They are noting whether the patient's engagement with the world is responsive and coherent or mechanical and diminished.
A person in deep coma has [Jing](./jing.md) (their body persists) and residual [Qi](./qi.md) (metabolic processes continue), but their Shen has withdrawn.
The body operates at a substrate level; it does not respond to its situation as a situation.

In the *Huang Di Nei Jing*, Shen is associated with the Heart (as a functional system).
When the Heart's Shen is settled, the person sleeps well, thinks clearly, responds to events with appropriate feeling, and can tolerate novelty without rigidity or collapse.
When Shen is disturbed — by emotional shock, chronic illness, or constitutional depletion — the person may be anxious, disoriented, or affectively flat.
The body continues to function, but its engagement with the world narrows [@unschuld2003].

Kristofer Schipper placed Shen within the Daoist cosmological framework as the most refined layer of vitality: Jing condenses into form, Qi animates that form, and Shen enables the animated form to be aware of itself and its situation [@schipper1993].
This is not a hierarchy of value but a hierarchy of refinement.
Shen depends on Qi (without operational activity, there is nothing to be aware of) and Qi depends on Jing (without a substrate, there are no operations to sustain).

The clinical significance is that Shen cannot be restored by adding more Qi.
A patient whose Qi is abundant but whose Shen is disturbed will be agitated, restless, operationally active but not coherently responsive.
The treatment addresses Shen directly — calming the Heart, settling the spirit — rather than increasing operational throughput.
More activity does not produce more awareness.

For information systems, Shen corresponds to what [second-order cybernetics](../../../../../../../../../../../information-science-services-section/services/cybernetics-services-section/content/text/glossary/terms/second-order-cybernetics.md) calls reflexive capacity and what [Argyris and Schön](../../../../../../../../../information-science-services-section/services/cybernetics-services-section/content/text/glossary/terms/single-loop-double-loop-learning.md) call double-loop learning: the ability to question whether the system's own categories, schemas, and operational frames still serve the situation they were built for.
A system with Shen does not just process data according to its schema.
It notices when the schema no longer fits — when the categories have drifted from the phenomena they classify, when the rules produce correct inferences from outdated premises.

This capacity is what the jiangshi lacks, and it is what no amount of operational sophistication can substitute for.

## Related terms

- [Jing](./jing.md) — stored substrate, the material foundation
- [Qi](./qi.md) — circulating energy, the operational layer
- [San Bao](./san-bao.md) — the Three Treasures as a diagnostic system
- [Second-order cybernetics](../../../../../../../../../../../information-science-services-section/services/cybernetics-services-section/content/text/glossary/terms/second-order-cybernetics.md) — the Western vocabulary closest to Shen
- [Single-loop and double-loop learning](../../../../../../../../../information-science-services-section/services/cybernetics-services-section/content/text/glossary/terms/single-loop-double-loop-learning.md) — reflexive capacity at the organizational level

records.name: Somatic Awareness
records.description: The trained capacity to attend to first-person bodily sensation as a source of information about posture, movement, and physiological state.

cites: Somatics: Reawakening the Mind's Control of Movement, Flexibility, and Health

hanna1988.title: Somatics: Reawakening the Mind's Control of Movement, Flexibility, and Health

records.body:
Somatic awareness is the trained capacity to attend to first-person bodily sensation — not as background noise but as structured information about posture, movement, tension, and physiological state.
It's the foundation on which all somatic practices build: before you can change a movement pattern, you have to feel it.

[Thomas Hanna](../../../../../../../../../../../information-science-services-section/services/knowledge-services-section/services/research-services-section/content/text/documents/articles/notes/thomas-hanna.md) distinguished somatic awareness from ordinary body consciousness.
Most people register their bodies only when something goes wrong — pain, fatigue, restriction.
Hanna argued that this reactive attention is a diminished version of what's possible.
Through practice, a person can develop continuous, fine-grained awareness of muscular tone, joint position, breathing rhythm, and visceral state [@hanna1988].
This isn't mystical sensitivity; it's the same perceptual capacity that musicians develop for pitch or winemakers develop for flavor — trained attention to sensory data that was always available but unattended.

## What somatic awareness tracks

Somatic awareness draws on multiple sensory systems simultaneously:

**[Proprioception](./proprioception.md)** — the sense of body position and movement.
Somatic awareness refines proprioceptive acuity: the capacity to feel small differences in joint angle, weight distribution, and muscular effort.
[Moshe Feldenkrais](../../../../../../../../../../../information-science-services-section/services/knowledge-services-section/services/research-services-section/content/text/documents/articles/notes/moshe-feldenkrais.md) demonstrated that reducing the intensity and speed of movement increases proprioceptive resolution [@feldenkrais1972].
This is why somatic lessons use slow, small movements — they're training the sensory system, not the muscles.

**[Interoception](./interoception.md)** — the sense of internal physiological state.
Heart rate, breathing depth, gut tension, thermal regulation.
[Stephen Porges](../../../../../../../../../../../information-science-services-section/services/knowledge-services-section/services/research-services-section/content/text/documents/articles/notes/stephen-porges.md)' polyvagal theory describes how interoceptive signals shape emotional state and social behavior [@porges2011].
Somatic awareness extends interoceptive acuity so that these signals become available to conscious attention rather than operating only through autonomic reflexes.

**Kinesthetic tone** — the felt quality of muscular engagement.
Not just "is this muscle contracted?" but "how contracted, with what quality, and in what relation to surrounding muscles?"
Hanna's concept of sensory-motor amnesia names the loss of this awareness: when habitual tension persists long enough, the cortex stops registering it.
The muscle is contracted, but the person can't feel it.
Somatic education reverses this amnesia by reintroducing voluntary control over the forgotten pattern.

## Sensory-motor amnesia

Hanna's central clinical concept is sensory-motor amnesia (SMA): the condition in which habitual muscular contraction drops below the threshold of conscious awareness.
SMA isn't a peripheral problem — the muscles work fine.
It's a cortical problem: the brain has stopped monitoring and voluntarily controlling the contraction pattern.

SMA develops through three reflexive patterns that Hanna identified:

- **The green-light reflex** — a pattern of posterior contraction (back extensors, hip flexors) associated with the Landau arousal response.
  Chronic activation produces the military posture: arched back, forward-thrust pelvis, compressed lumbar spine.
- **The red-light reflex** — a pattern of anterior contraction (abdominals, chest flexors, neck flexors) associated with the startle response.
  Chronic activation produces the slumped, protective posture: rounded shoulders, compressed chest, forward head.
- **The trauma reflex** — a lateral pattern of contraction on one side of the body, typically following injury or asymmetric habitual use.
  Produces lateral tilt, hip hiking, and rotational distortion.

These patterns compound over time.
A person who has accumulated green-light, red-light, and trauma reflexes doesn't feel tense — they feel normal.
The tension has become invisible to their own nervous system.
Somatic awareness practices make it visible again, and [pandiculation](./pandiculation.md) provides the mechanism for releasing it.

## Relation to clinical assessment

Somatic awareness doesn't replace clinical assessment; it supplements it.
A clinician observes the body from outside — posture analysis, range-of-motion testing, imaging.
Somatic awareness provides the inside view: what the person actually feels in their body, which may not match what external observation predicts.

This discrepancy is itself diagnostic.
When a person reports no tension in muscles that are visibly contracted, that's sensory-motor amnesia.
When a person reports pain in a region where no structural pathology exists, that's a signal about cortical motor-sensory processing, not peripheral tissue damage.
Somatic awareness makes these discrepancies articulable.

## Related concepts

- [Proprioception](./proprioception.md) — the sensory substrate for spatial body awareness
- [Interoception](./interoception.md) — the sensory substrate for internal-state awareness
- [Pandiculation](./pandiculation.md) — the technique for reversing sensory-motor amnesia
- [Somatic Experiencing](./somatic-experiencing.md) — a trauma approach that depends on somatic awareness capacity
- [Disability justice](../../../../../../content/text/glossary/terms/disability-justice.md) — framework that insists on first-person authority over one's own embodiment
- [Tensegrity in Movement](./tensegrity-in-movement.md) — the structural model that somatic awareness attends to from within

## Sources

- Hanna, T.
  (1988).
  *Somatics: Reawakening the Mind's Control of Movement, Flexibility, and Health.*
  Addison-Wesley [@hanna1988].
- Feldenkrais, M.
  (1972).
  *Awareness Through Movement.*
  Harper & Row [@feldenkrais1972].
- Porges, S.W. (2011).
  *The Polyvagal Theory.*
  Norton [@porges2011].

records.name: Somatic Experiencing
records.description: Peter Levine's body-oriented trauma resolution method, grounded in tracking the felt sense of incomplete defensive responses.

cites: In an Unspoken Voice: How the Body Releases Trauma and Restores Goodness

levine2010.title: In an Unspoken Voice: How the Body Releases Trauma and Restores Goodness

records.body:
Somatic Experiencing (SE) is a body-oriented approach to trauma resolution developed by [Peter Levine](../../../../../../../../../../../information-science-services-section/services/knowledge-services-section/services/research-services-section/content/text/documents/articles/notes/peter-levine.md).
Its core claim: trauma isn't stored as a memory in the cognitive sense but as an incomplete physiological response — a defensive action (fight, flight, freeze) that the nervous system initiated but couldn't complete.
Resolution comes not from narrating the event but from allowing the body to complete the interrupted response through careful, titrated attention to [somatic awareness](./somatic-awareness.md) [@levine1997].

## The biological basis

Levine's starting observation comes from ethology.
Prey animals routinely survive life-threatening encounters and return to normal function within minutes.
After a gazelle escapes a predator and reaches safety, its body goes through a discharge sequence — trembling, shaking, deep breathing — that completes the physiological cycle of the threat response.
The nervous system activates the sympathetic fight-or-flight response, and when the threat passes, the parasympathetic system completes the cycle through discharge and restoration.

Humans, Levine argues, frequently interrupt this cycle.
Social conditioning, medical intervention, immobilization (as in car accidents or surgical procedures), and cognitive override ("I should be over this") prevent the discharge phase from completing.
The sympathetic activation remains bound in the nervous system — not as a thought but as a physiological state.
The person may not consciously remember the event, but their body continues to produce the defensive response: chronic tension, hypervigilance, dissociation, autonomic dysregulation.

[Stephen Porges](../../../../../../../../../../../information-science-services-section/services/knowledge-services-section/services/research-services-section/content/text/documents/articles/notes/stephen-porges.md)' polyvagal theory provides a neuroanatomical framework for this process.
The vagal system mediates three hierarchical response states: ventral vagal (social engagement, safety), sympathetic (mobilization, fight-or-flight), and dorsal vagal (immobilization, shutdown) [@porges2011].
Trauma, in SE terms, is a nervous system stuck in sympathetic activation or dorsal vagal shutdown — unable to return to the ventral vagal state that supports social engagement and recovery.

## The method

SE sessions don't require detailed narration of traumatic events.
The practitioner guides the client's attention to bodily sensations — warmth, tightness, trembling, numbness, pulsing — and tracks the body's responses as they arise.
The method relies on several core techniques:

**Titration.**
Rather than flooding the system with traumatic material, SE approaches the activation in small doses.
The client touches the edge of the activation, notices what the body does, and then returns to a resource state before proceeding further.
This prevents retraumatization and keeps the nervous system within a window where processing can occur.

**Pendulation.**
The natural rhythm of the nervous system oscillates between states of activation and settling.
SE works with this rhythm, guiding the client to notice the movement between contraction and expansion, tension and release.
Over time, the pendulation widens: the system accesses deeper layers of held activation while maintaining the capacity to return to regulation.

**Felt sense.**
SE tracks what [Eugene Gendlin](../../../../../../../../../../../information-science-services-section/services/knowledge-services-section/services/research-services-section/content/text/documents/articles/notes/eugene-gendlin.md) called the "felt sense" — the holistic, bodily sense of a situation that precedes and exceeds cognitive understanding [@gendlin1978].
In SE, the felt sense is the primary data: not what the client thinks about the event, but what their body does when the event's activation arises.
Shifts in the felt sense — from contraction to flow, from numbness to sensation, from rigidity to trembling — indicate that the nervous system is completing its interrupted response.

**Discharge.**
When the bound activation begins to release, the body produces involuntary responses: trembling, shaking, deep breathing, yawning, temperature changes, waves of sensation.
These aren't symptoms to be managed; they're the completion of the defensive cycle that was interrupted.
The practitioner's role is to support the client in allowing discharge to occur without cognitive interference.

## Relation to other somatic concepts

SE depends on the capacities that other somatic practices develop.
[Interoceptive](./interoception.md) acuity — the ability to detect and track internal physiological states — is the perceptual skill that SE sessions train and rely on.
[Proprioceptive](./proprioception.md) awareness supports the recognition of held defensive postures: the braced shoulders, the retracted pelvis, the clenched jaw that persist as residues of incomplete fight-or-flight responses.

SE also connects to the vault's [harm reduction](../../../../../public-health-services-section/content/text/glossary/terms/harm-reduction.md) framework.
SE doesn't demand that a person revisit or narrate their worst experiences.
It meets the nervous system where it is and works within the system's current capacity.
This is harm reduction applied to trauma treatment: reduce the immediate physiological consequences of unresolved activation without requiring conditions (narrative coherence, emotional readiness, therapeutic alliance) that may not yet exist.

## Related concepts

- [Somatic Awareness](./somatic-awareness.md) — the foundational capacity that SE trains and depends on
- [Interoception](./interoception.md) — the sensory channel through which SE tracks nervous system state
- [Pandiculation](./pandiculation.md) — a related but distinct mechanism for releasing held muscular patterns
- [Harm reduction](../../../../../public-health-services-section/content/text/glossary/terms/harm-reduction.md) — the principle of meeting people where they are, which SE applies to trauma treatment
- [Disability justice](../../../../../../content/text/glossary/terms/disability-justice.md) — framework for understanding how trauma and embodiment intersect with structural conditions

## Sources

- Levine, P.
  (1997).
  *Waking the Tiger: Healing Trauma.*
  North Atlantic Books [@levine1997].
- Levine, P.
  (2010).
  *In an Unspoken Voice: How the Body Releases Trauma and Restores Goodness.*
  North Atlantic Books [@levine2010].
- Gendlin, E.T. (1978).
  *Focusing.*
  Everest House [@gendlin1978].
- Porges, S.W. (2011).
  *The Polyvagal Theory.*
  Norton [@porges2011].

records.name: Stilbenoid
records.description: A class of polyphenolic compounds based on a 1,2-diphenylethylene backbone, produced by plants as phytoalexins — including resveratrol, the compound that made Japanese knotweed pharmacologically significant
records.body:
Stilbenoids are a class of [polyphenolic](polyphenol.md) compounds based on a 1,2-diphenylethylene (stilbene) backbone — two phenyl rings connected by a two-carbon ethylene bridge. They are produced by plants primarily as [phytoalexins](phytoalexin.md) — defensive compounds synthesized in response to pathogen attack, UV radiation, or tissue injury. Stilbenoids are synthesized via the phenylpropanoid pathway from phenylalanine, with stilbene synthase catalyzing the final cyclization step.

## Key stilbenoid compounds

**[Resveratrol](resveratrol.md)** (*trans*-3,5,4'-trihydroxystilbene): The most studied stilbenoid. Produced in large quantities by [Japanese knotweed](../../../../../../../botany-services-section/content/text/glossary/terms/japanese-knotweed.md) rhizome, grape skins, peanuts, and blueberries. Inhibits platelet aggregation, NF-κB, COX-2, and activates AMPK and SIRT1 pathways.

**Polydatin** (piceid): The glucoside form of resveratrol — resveratrol bonded to a glucose molecule. The predominant stilbenoid in Japanese knotweed rhizome. Better oral [bioavailability](bioavailability.md) than free resveratrol due to potential intestinal transport via SGLT1.

**Piceatannol**: A hydroxylated derivative of resveratrol with stronger antioxidant and immunomodulatory activity. Found in grapes, passion fruit, and knotweed.

**Pterostilbene**: A dimethylated analogue of resveratrol found primarily in blueberries. Higher oral bioavailability than resveratrol due to reduced susceptibility to glucuronidation.

## Distribution

Stilbenoid production is concentrated in a few plant families: Vitaceae (grapes), [Polygonaceae](../../../../../../../botany-services-section/content/text/glossary/terms/polygonaceae.md) (knotweeds, rhubarb), Fabaceae (peanuts), and Dipterocarpaceae (tropical timber trees). Japanese knotweed produces stilbenoids at concentrations 50–100 times higher than grape skins, making it the primary commercial source for resveratrol supplements.

## See also

- [Resveratrol](resveratrol.md) — the most studied member
- [Polyphenol](polyphenol.md) — the parent chemical class
- [Phytoalexin](phytoalexin.md) — the defensive function that drives stilbenoid production
- [Japanese Knotweed](../../../../../../../botany-services-section/content/text/glossary/terms/japanese-knotweed.md) — the richest natural source

records.name: Stomach
records.description: Wèi: the yang organ of Chinese medicine that receives food and drink and 'rots and ripens' them, sending its contents downward; the Spleen's partner in making qi and blood.

maciocia2015.title: The Foundations of Chinese Medicine: A Comprehensive Text

records.body:
The Stomach (胃, wèi) is a yang, or fu, organ of [zang-fu](./zang-fu.md) theory, paired with the [Spleen](./spleen.md) in the earth phase of [wu xing](./wu-xing.md). It receives food and drink and "rots and ripens" them, the first stage of digestion, from which the Spleen extracts the refined essence that becomes [qi](./qi.md) and [blood](./xue.md) [@maciocia2015].

Its qi moves downward. When it rises instead, the result is nausea, belching, hiccup or vomiting (rebellious Stomach qi). It is also called the origin of fluids, and a dry mouth and tongue are among the signs of Stomach yin deficiency. The Spleen moves upward and prefers dryness; the Stomach moves downward and prefers moisture. Much of Chinese dietetics is written for keeping the two in balance.

records.name: Stridor
records.description: A high-pitched, often inspiratory respiratory sound produced by turbulent airflow through a narrowed upper airway, indicating obstruction at or above the vocal cords.
records.body:
**Stridor** is a high-pitched respiratory sound, often inspiratory, that raises concern for upper-[airway](./airway.md) narrowing. It is produced by turbulent airflow through a narrowed segment of the airway above or at the level of the vocal cords.

The timing of stridor within the respiratory cycle provides diagnostic information:

- **Inspiratory stridor** — suggests obstruction at or above the vocal cords (supraglottic): epiglottitis, croup, foreign body in the pharynx, angioedema, peritonsillar abscess
- **Expiratory stridor** — suggests obstruction below the vocal cords (subglottic): tracheal stenosis, foreign body in the trachea
- **Biphasic stridor** (both inspiratory and expiratory) — suggests a fixed obstruction at the level of the vocal cords or subglottis: severe croup, vocal cord paralysis, subglottic stenosis

Stridor is a clinical sign, not a diagnosis. Its presence indicates that the upper airway is significantly narrowed — typically to less than 50% of its normal diameter before stridor becomes audible. This means that by the time stridor is heard, the obstruction is already substantial.

The clinical urgency of stridor depends on context. Stridor in a child with a barking cough and low-grade fever suggests croup and may respond to nebulized epinephrine and dexamethasone. Stridor in an adult with lip swelling and urticaria after a medication exposure suggests anaphylaxis and requires immediate epinephrine and preparation for possible intubation. Stridor that is worsening, associated with drooling or inability to swallow, or accompanied by signs of respiratory failure (accessory muscle use, cyanosis, altered mental status) demands immediate airway intervention.

Stridor should be distinguished from [wheeze](./wheeze.md), which is typically expiratory and indicates lower-airway narrowing. Both are sounds of turbulent airflow through a narrowed passage, but their anatomical location and clinical implications differ.

## Related terms

- [Wheeze](./wheeze.md) — lower-airway narrowing sound
- [Airway](./airway.md) — the passage whose narrowing produces stridor
- [CICO](./cannot-intubate-cannot-oxygenate.md) — the emergency that severe upper-airway obstruction can produce
